title.zh: 卷二百一十 列傳第一百三十五 藩鎮魏博
title.raw: 卷二百一十 列傳第一百三十五 藩鎮魏博 Volume 210 Biographies 135: Buffer Region Weibo

sentences.zh: 藩鎮魏博

translations.literal: Buffer Regions: Weibo
translations.idiomatic: Buffer Regions — Weibo

sentences.zh: 安、史亂天下，至肅宗大難略平，君臣皆幸安，故瓜分河北地，付授叛將，護養孽萌，以成禍根。

translations.literal: An [Lushan] and Shi [Siming] threw the realm into chaos; by the time Emperor Suzong had largely quelled the great calamity, sovereign and ministers alike rejoiced in peace, and so they carved up the lands of Hebei and entrusted them to renegade generals, nurturing the seeds of disaster until they took root.
translations.idiomatic: The An and Shi rebellions convulsed the empire. When Emperor Suzong had at last brought the greatest catastrophe roughly to an end, court and throne alike were so grateful for stability that they partitioned Hebei and handed its territories to defecting commanders — sheltering rebellious seedlings until they grew into enduring ruin.

sentences.zh: 亂人乘之，遂擅署吏，以賦稅自私，不朝獻於廷。

translations.literal: Disordered men seized the opportunity; they then appointed officials on their own authority, kept tax revenues for themselves, and did not present tribute at court.
translations.idiomatic: The unruly seized their chance. They appointed officials at will, pocketed tax revenues for themselves, and ceased sending tribute to the capital.

sentences.zh: 效戰國，肱髀相依，以土地傳子孫，脅百姓，加鋸其頸，利怵逆汙，遂使其人自視猶羌狄然。

translations.literal: Emulating the Warring States, they leaned upon one another like arm and thigh, passing land to sons and grandsons; they coerced the common people, put the saw to their necks, lured and terrified them into crime and debauchery, until those folk came to see themselves as no different from barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Like the warring kingdoms of old, they braced one another — arm and thigh — bequeathing territory from father to son. They terrorized the populace, pressed the blade to their throats, and tempted and frightened them into crime and corruption, until the people came to regard themselves as little better than barbarians.

sentences.zh: 一寇死，一賊生，訖唐亡百餘年，卒不為王土。

translations.literal: One bandit died, another thief arose; through more than a century until Tang's fall, the land never became royal domain.
translations.idiomatic: One outlaw fell, another rose in his place. For more than a century until the Tang collapsed, the region never again became true imperial soil.

sentences.zh: 當其盛時，蔡附齊連，內裂河南地，為合從以抗天子。

translations.literal: At their height, Cai [State] attached itself to Qi and linked with it, splitting the lands south of the Yellow River within, forming alliances to resist the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: At their height, the buffer lords of Cai clung to Qi and forged chains of alliance, carving up the lands south of the Yellow River and banding together to defy the throne.

sentences.zh: 杜牧至以「山東，王不得，不王；

translations.literal: Du Mu went so far as to say, 'East of the mountains — without it one cannot become king;
translations.idiomatic: Du Mu went so far as to declare, 'East of the mountains — without it one cannot become king;

sentences.zh: 霸不得，不霸；

translations.literal: without it one cannot become hegemon;
translations.idiomatic: without it one cannot become hegemon;

sentences.zh: 賊得之，故天下不安」。

translations.literal: the rebels hold it, and so the realm is not at peace.'
translations.idiomatic: the rebels hold it, and so the realm knows no peace.'

sentences.zh: 又曰：

translations.literal: He also said:
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote:

sentences.zh: 厥今天下何如哉？

translations.literal: What is the realm like today?
translations.idiomatic: What has become of the empire?

sentences.zh: 幹戈朽，斧鉞鈍，含引混貸，照育逆孽，殆為故常。

translations.literal: Spears and halberds lie rusted, axes and executioner's blades grow dull; tolerance and forbearance are extended indiscriminately, nurturing rebellious offspring as though it were custom.
translations.idiomatic: Spears lie rusted, executioners' axes dull; indulgence and leniency are lavished on traitors until rebellion itself seems ordinary.

sentences.zh: 而執事大人曾不歷算周思，以為宿謀，方且嵬岸抑揚，自以為廣大繁昌莫己若也。

translations.literal: Yet you gentlemen in office have never once reckoned and pondered this as a long-standing design; instead you stand on lofty banks, vaunting yourselves, believing none so vast and flourishing as you.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you who hold power never reckon this as a deliberate strategy long in the making. Instead you stand on your high banks, swelling with pride, convinced that none is so vast and prosperous as yourselves.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 其不知乎，其俟蹇頓顛傾而後為之支計乎？

translations.literal: Do you not know? Or do you wait until ruin and collapse before devising remedies?
translations.idiomatic: Do you not see? Or will you wait until disaster and collapse force you to act?

sentences.zh: 且天下幾裏，列郡幾所，自河以北，蟠城數百，角奔為寇，伺吾人憔悴，天時不利，則將與其朋伍駭亂吾民於掌股之上。

translations.literal: Moreover, how many li does the realm span, how many commanderies does it contain? From the Yellow River northward, walled cities number in the hundreds; they charge about as bandits, watching for our people to grow weary and the seasons to turn against us, then with their comrades they will terrify and harry our folk as easily as clapping hands upon the thigh.
translations.idiomatic: Consider the empire's extent — how many leagues, how many prefectures? North of the Yellow River alone stand hundreds of walled cities. They raid at will, watching for our people to grow exhausted and fortune to turn, then with their allies they will terrorize the populace as easily as striking palm against thigh.

sentences.zh: 今者及吾之壯，不圖擒取，乃偷處恬逸，以為後世子孫背脅疽根，此復何也？

translations.literal: Now, while we are still strong, you do not plan to seize them; instead you dwell in ease and comfort, bequeathing to later generations a tumor at the back that will fester — what is this?
translations.idiomatic: While we still have strength, you refuse to strike and capture them. Instead you settle into complacent ease, leaving posterity a festering abscess at the spine — what folly is this?

sentences.zh: 議者曰：倔強之徒，吾以良將勁兵為銜策，高位美爵充飽其腸，安而不橈，外而不拘，猶豢虎狼而不拂其心，則忿氣不萌，此大歷、貞元所以守邦也。

translations.literal: Those who argue say: These stubborn fellows — we hold them with fine generals and strong troops as bit and reins, fill their bellies with high rank and splendid titles, and they remain secure without bending, outwardly compliant without restraint — like raising tigers and wolves without rousing their hearts, so that wrath never sprouts. This is how the Dali and Zhenyuan reigns preserved the state.
translations.idiomatic: The advocates of appeasement say: These stubborn warlords — we hold them with elite generals and crack troops as bit and bridle, sate them with high office and glittering honors, and they remain docile without rebellion, outwardly obedient without constraint — like keeping tigers and wolves without stirring their savage hearts, so that fury never takes root. Thus did the Dali and Zhenyuan eras preserve the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 何必疾戰焚煎吾民，然後為快也？

translations.literal: Why must we hasten to battle and burn our people before we can feel satisfaction?
translations.idiomatic: Why must we rush to war and scorch our own people before we can feel at ease?

sentences.zh: 愚曰：大歷、貞元之間，有城數十，千百卒夫，則朝廷貸以法，故於是闊視大言，自樹一家，破制削法，角為尊奢。

translations.literal: The foolish reply: Between the Dali and Zhenyuan reigns, when there were dozens of cities and thousands upon thousands of garrison troops, the court indulged them with lax enforcement of law; therefore they looked about with bold speech, established themselves as separate houses, broke regulations and pared away statutes, and vied in arrogance and extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: The answer is folly itself: Under Dali and Zhenyuan, when dozens of cities and thousands of soldiers answered to these lords, the court indulged them with slack enforcement of law. They grew bold in speech, set themselves up as sovereign houses, tore down regulations, and competed in arrogance and excess.

sentences.zh: 天子不問，有司不呵；

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven did not inquire; the responsible offices did not rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor never questioned them; the responsible ministries never rebuked them.

sentences.zh: 王侯通爵，越錄受之；

translations.literal: Princes and marquises exchanged noble ranks; they received appointments beyond their proper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and marquises traded noble titles; they received appointments far above their proper rank.

sentences.zh: 覲聘不來，幾杖扶之；

translations.literal: They did not come for audience; the court sent walking-sticks to support them.
translations.idiomatic: They skipped imperial audiences; the court sent them ceremonial staffs to ease their infirmity.

sentences.zh: 逆息虜胤，皇子嬪之。

translations.literal: Rebellious offspring and captive heirs — imperial sons and daughters were given to them in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellious scions and captive heirs — imperial princes and princesses were married into their families.

sentences.zh: 地益廣，兵益強，僭擬益甚，侈心益昌。

translations.literal: Territory grew broader, armies stronger, presumption more extreme, and extravagant ambition more unchecked.
translations.idiomatic: Their domains widened, their armies swelled, their pretensions grew bolder, and their appetite for luxury ran ever wilder.

sentences.zh: 土田名器，分劃大盡，而賊夫貪心，未及畔岸，淫名越號，走兵四略，以飽其誌。

translations.literal: Land, population, and insignia of office were divided to the utmost, yet the bandits' greedy hearts, before they reached open revolt, already exceeded their titles, usurped ranks, and sent armies in four directions to satisfy their ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: Land, population, and symbols of office were parceled out to the limit — yet even before open rebellion, their greed outran their titles. They seized unlawful ranks and sent armies in every direction to feed their ambitions.

sentences.zh: 趙、魏、燕、齊，同日而起，梁、蔡、吳、蜀，躡而和之，其餘混澒軒囂，欲相效者，往往而是。

translations.literal: Zhao, Wei, Yan, and Qi rose on the same day; Liang, Cai, Wu, and Shu followed in accord; the rest, churning and clamoring, wishing to imitate them, were everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, Wei, Yan, and Qi rose together in a single day; Liang, Cai, Wu, and Shu joined in their wake. Everywhere others churned and clamored, eager to follow their example.

sentences.zh: 運遭孝武，前英後傑，夕思朝議，故能大者誅鉏，小者惠來。

translations.literal: Fortune then favored Emperor Xiaowu; worthy men came before and after, pondering by night and deliberating by day — and so the great were executed and uprooted, the small were won over with grace.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune then smiled on Emperor Xiaowu. Worthies served him in succession, debating policy night and day — and so the greatest rebels were cut down, the lesser brought back with clemency.

sentences.zh: 大抵生人油然多欲，欲而不得則怒，怒則爭亂隨之。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, the living are naturally full of desire; when desire is denied, anger follows, and with anger comes strife and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Human nature brims with desire. Denied what they want, men grow angry — and anger breeds strife and chaos.

sentences.zh: 是以教笞於家，刑罰於國，征伐於天下，裁其欲而塞其爭也。

translations.literal: Therefore there is instruction and beating in the home, punishment and law in the state, and campaigns under Heaven — to trim desire and block strife.
translations.idiomatic: Hence instruction and discipline within the household, law and punishment within the state, and campaigns across the realm — all to curb desire and choke off conflict.

sentences.zh: 大歷、貞元之間反此，提區區之有，而塞無涯之爭，是以首尾指支，幾不能相運掉也。

translations.literal: The Dali and Zhenyuan reigns reversed this: holding a tiny measure of possessions while blocking boundless contention — and so head, tail, fingers, and limbs could scarcely move in concert.
translations.idiomatic: Dali and Zhenyuan reversed this wisdom: clutching a meager share while trying to dam an ocean of ambition — until head, tail, fingers, and limbs could scarcely act as one body.

sentences.zh: 凡今者不知非此，而反用以為經，將見為盜者非止於河北而已。

translations.literal: Those today do not recognize this error, but instead take it as constant principle — and will find that the bandits are not confined to Hebei alone.
translations.idiomatic: Men today fail to see this error and instead treat it as eternal doctrine — and will discover that rebellion is not confined to Hebei alone.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 大歷、貞元守邦之術，永戒之哉！

translations.literal: The art of preserving the state under Dali and Zhenyuan — let it be an everlasting warning!
translations.idiomatic: The methods by which Dali and Zhenyuan preserved the dynasty — let them stand as an everlasting warning!

sentences.zh: 魏博傳五世，至田弘正入朝，十年復亂，更四姓，傳十世，有州七。

translations.literal: Weibo passed through five generations until Tian Hongzheng entered court; ten years later chaos returned; four surnames changed in succession; it endured ten generations and held seven prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Weibo passed through five generations until Tian Hongzheng submitted to the court; ten years later rebellion returned. Four ruling clans succeeded one another across ten generations, holding seven prefectures.

sentences.zh: 成德更二姓，傳五世，至王承元入朝明年，王廷湊反，傳六世，有州四。

translations.literal: Chengde changed two surnames and passed through five generations until Wang Chengyuan entered court; the next year Wang Tingcou rebelled; it endured six generations and held four prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Chengde saw two ruling clans across five generations until Wang Chengyuan submitted; the following year Wang Tingcou rebelled. The domain endured six generations and held four prefectures.

sentences.zh: 盧龍更三姓，傳五世，至劉總入朝，六月，朱克融反，傳十二世，有州九。

translations.literal: Lulong changed three surnames and passed through five generations until Liu Zong entered court; six months later Zhu Kerong rebelled; it endured twelve generations and held nine prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Lulong saw three ruling clans across five generations until Liu Zong submitted; six months later Zhu Kerong rebelled. The domain endured twelve generations and held nine prefectures.

sentences.zh: 淄青傳五世而滅，有州十二。

translations.literal: Ziqing passed through five generations and perished, holding twelve prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Ziqing lasted five generations before falling, holding twelve prefectures.

sentences.zh: 滄景傳三世，至程權入朝，十六年而李全略有之，至其子同捷而滅，有州四。

translations.literal: Cangjing passed through three generations until Cheng Quan entered court; sixteen years later Li Quanlue seized it; it ended with his son Tongjie, holding four prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Cangjing passed through three generations until Cheng Quan submitted; sixteen years later Li Quanlue seized control. The domain fell with his son Tongjie, holding four prefectures.

sentences.zh: 宣武傳四世而滅，有州四。

translations.literal: Xuanwu passed through four generations and perished, holding four prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanwu lasted four generations before falling, holding four prefectures.

sentences.zh: 彰義傳三世而滅，有州三。

translations.literal: Zhangyi passed through three generations and perished, holding three prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangyi lasted three generations before falling, holding three prefectures.

sentences.zh: 澤潞傳三世而滅，有州五。

translations.literal: Zelu passed through three generations and perished, holding five prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Zelu lasted three generations before falling, holding five prefectures.

sentences.zh: 雖然，跡其由來，事有因藉，地之輕重，視人謀臧否歟！

translations.literal: Even so, tracing their origins, affairs had their causes; whether territory weighed heavy or light depended on the wisdom or folly of the men involved!
translations.idiomatic: Even so, tracing their origins, each rise had its causes. Whether a domain grew heavy or light in the balance depended on the wisdom or folly of the men who held it!

sentences.zh: 今取擅興若世嗣者，為《藩鎮傳》。

translations.literal: Here we take those who rose on their own authority or inherited rule by generation, and compose the 'Biographies of Buffer Regions.'
translations.idiomatic: Here we treat those who seized power on their own authority or passed it down through successive generations, composing the Biographies of Buffer Regions.

sentences.zh: 若田弘正、張孝忠等，暴忠納誠，以屏王室，自如別傳雲。

translations.literal: As for Tian Hongzheng, Zhang Xiaozhong, and the like, who displayed fierce loyalty and offered sincerity to shield the royal house — they are treated in separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: As for Tian Hongzheng, Zhang Xiaozhong, and others who showed fierce loyalty and offered their sincerity to shield the throne — they receive separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 田承嗣，字承嗣，平州盧龍人。

translations.literal: Tian Chengsi, courtesy name Chengsi, was a native of Ping Prefecture in Lulong.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chengsi, courtesy name Chengsi, was a native of Pingzhou in Lulong.

sentences.zh: 世事盧龍軍，以豪俠聞。

translations.literal: His family had served for generations in the Lulong army and was known for bold chivalry.
translations.idiomatic: His family had served for generations in the Lulong army and was renowned for bold chivalry.

sentences.zh: 隸安祿山麾下，破奚、契丹，累功至武衛將軍。

translations.literal: He served under An Lushan, defeated the Xi and Khitan, and through accumulated merit rose to General of Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He served under An Lushan, defeated the Xi and Khitan tribes, and through accumulated merit rose to General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 祿山反，與張忠誌為賊前驅，陷河、洛。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, he and Zhang Zhizhi served as the rebels' vanguard and captured the lands of the Yellow River and Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled, he and Zhang Zhizhi served as the rebels' vanguard, conquering the lands between the Yellow River and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 嘗大雪，祿山按行諸屯，至其營，若無人，已而擐甲列卒，閱所籍，不缺一人，祿山異其能，使守潁川。

translations.literal: Once, in heavy snow, Lushan inspected the encampments; when he reached Chengsi's camp it seemed deserted, but presently armored soldiers lined up in ranks; checking the register, not one man was missing. Lushan marveled at his ability and made him defend Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Once, in heavy snow, Lushan inspected the camps. Chengsi's quarters seemed empty — yet in a moment armored soldiers stood ranked in formation. Checking the rolls, not a single man was absent. Lushan marveled at his discipline and appointed him to defend Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀平東都，承嗣以郡降，俄而復叛。

translations.literal: When Guo Ziyi pacified the eastern capital, Chengsi surrendered the commandery, but soon rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Ziyi pacified the eastern capital, Chengsi surrendered his commandery — then rebelled again almost at once.

sentences.zh: 安慶緒奔鄴，承嗣自潁川來，與蔡希德、武令榔合兵六萬，慶緒復振，抗王師。

translations.literal: An Qingxu fled to Ye; Chengsi came from Yingchuan and joined Cai Xide and Wu Linglang with sixty thousand troops; Qingxu revived his fortunes and resisted the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: When An Qingxu fled to Ye, Chengsi marched from Yingchuan and joined Cai Xide and Wu Linglang with sixty thousand men. Qingxu rallied his forces and stood against the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，史思明亂，承嗣又為賊導，及朝義敗，與共保莫州。

translations.literal: After more than a year Shi Siming revolted; Chengsi again served as the rebels' guide; when Chaoyi was defeated, they together held Mo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later, when Shi Siming rebelled, Chengsi again guided the rebel armies. When Shi Chaoyi was defeated, they held Mo Prefecture together.

sentences.zh: 仆固玚追北，承嗣急，乃詐朝義使自求救幽州。

translations.literal: Pugu Chang pursued northward; Chengsi, pressed hard, then feigned that Chaoyi had sent him to seek rescue from Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Chang pressed the pursuit northward. Hard pressed, Chengsi feigned that Chaoyi had dispatched him to seek relief from Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 承嗣守莫，因執賊妻息降於玚，厚以金帛反間玚將士。

translations.literal: Chengsi held Mo while seizing the rebels' wives and children to surrender to Chang, and lavishly used gold and silk to sow discord among Chang's officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi held Mo Prefecture, seized the rebels' wives and children, and surrendered them to Chang — while lavishing gold and silk to sow discord among Chang's officers and men.

sentences.zh: 玚慮下生變，即約降。

translations.literal: Chang, fearing mutiny below, then agreed to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, fearing mutiny in the ranks, agreed to accept the surrender.

sentences.zh: 承嗣詐疾不出，玚欲馳入取之，承嗣列千刀為備，玚不得誌，承嗣重賂之以免。

translations.literal: Chengsi feigned illness and would not come out; Chang wished to ride in and seize him; Chengsi arrayed a thousand blades in readiness, and Chang could not achieve his aim. Chengsi bribed him heavily and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi feigned illness and refused to emerge. Chang tried to ride in and seize him, but Chengsi lined up a thousand swords in readiness and Chang could not carry out his plan. Chengsi bribed him lavishly and escaped.

sentences.zh: 乃與張忠誌、李懷仙、薛嵩皆詣仆固懷恩謝，願備行間。

translations.literal: Then he, together with Zhang Zhizhi, Li Huaixian, and Xue Song, all went to Pugu Huai'en to apologize and asked to serve on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Zhang Zhizhi, Li Huaixian, and Xue Song in presenting themselves to Pugu Huai'en to apologize and offer to serve on campaign.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以二賊繼亂，州縣殘析，數大赦，凡為賊詿誤，一切不問。

translations.literal: The court, because the two rebels had stirred chaos in succession and counties and prefectures lay in ruins, repeatedly issued great amnesties; all who had been misled into serving the rebels were entirely excused.
translations.idiomatic: The court, seeing how the two rebel regimes had ravaged the land in succession until counties and prefectures lay in ruins, issued repeated great amnesties. All who had been misled into serving the rebels were fully pardoned.

sentences.zh: 當是時，懷恩功高，亦恐賊平則任不重，因建白承嗣等分帥河北，賜鐵券，誓不死。

translations.literal: At that time Huai'en's merit was high, yet he also feared that once the rebels were pacified his responsibilities would no longer weigh heavily; therefore he proposed that Chengsi and the others divide command of Hebei, granting them iron certificates swearing they would not be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en's achievements were then at their height, yet he feared that once the rebels fell his importance would fade. He therefore proposed that Chengsi and the others divide command of Hebei, granting them iron certificates pledging they would not be executed.

sentences.zh: 拜承嗣莫州刺史，三遷至貝博滄瀛等州節度使，檢校太尉。

translations.literal: Chengsi was appointed prefect of Mo Prefecture, and through three promotions became military commissioner of Bei, Bo, Cang, Ying, and other prefectures, with the honorary title of Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi was appointed prefect of Mo Prefecture, then promoted thrice to military commissioner of Bei, Bo, Cang, Ying, and neighboring prefectures, with the honorary title of Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 承嗣沈猜陰賊，不習禮義。

translations.literal: Chengsi was deep, suspicious, and secretly treacherous, unversed in ritual and propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi was deep, suspicious, and secretly treacherous, untrained in ritual and propriety.

sentences.zh: 既得誌，即計戶口，重賦斂，歷兵繕甲，使老弱耕，壯者在軍，不數年，有眾十萬。

translations.literal: Once his ambition was fulfilled, he immediately counted households, imposed heavy taxation, drilled troops and repaired armor, set the old and weak to farming and the strong to the army; within a few years he had a hundred thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Once secure in power, he immediately registered households, imposed heavy taxes, drilled troops and repaired armor, set the old and weak to farming and the able-bodied to the ranks. Within a few years he commanded a hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 又擇趫秀強力者萬人，號牙兵，自署置官吏，圖版稅入，皆私有之。

translations.literal: He also selected ten thousand of the swiftest, finest, and strongest, calling them the 'Tooth Army'; he appointed officials on his own authority, and kept land registers and tax revenues as private property.
translations.idiomatic: He also selected ten thousand of the swiftest, finest, and strongest men, calling them the Tooth Army. He appointed officials on his own authority and kept land registers and tax revenues for himself alone.

sentences.zh: 又求兼宰相，代宗以寇亂甫平，多所含宥，因就加同中書門下平章事，封雁門郡王，寵其軍曰天雄，以魏州為大都督府，即授長史，詔子華尚永樂公主，冀結其心。

translations.literal: He further sought to hold the post of chief minister concurrently; Emperor Daizong, because the rebel turmoil had only just been pacified and indulgence was widespread, thereupon added the title of Co-Director of the Department of State Affairs with the Secretariat, enfeoffed him as Prince of Yanmen, favored his army with the name Tianxiong, made Weizhou the great protectorate capital, and immediately appointed him chief administrator; an edict also gave his son Hua in marriage to the Princess of Yongle, hoping to bind his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: He further sought the concurrent post of chief minister. Emperor Daizong, with rebellion only just suppressed and leniency the order of the day, granted him the title Co-Director of the Department of State Affairs with the Secretariat, enfeoffed him as Prince of Yanmen, named his army the Tianxiong, made Weizhou the great protectorate capital, and appointed him chief administrator on the spot. An edict also married his son Hua to the Princess of Yongle, hoping to win his heart.

sentences.zh: 而性著兇詭，愈不遜。

translations.literal: But his nature was marked by violence and cunning; he became all the more insubordinate.
translations.idiomatic: But violence and cunning were stamped on his nature, and he grew ever more insubordinate.

sentences.zh: 大歷八年，相衛薛嵩死，弟萼求假節，牙將裴誌清逐萼，萼以眾歸承嗣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of the Dali reign, Xue Song of Xiang and Wei died; his younger brother E requested acting commission; the tooth general Pei Zhiqing drove E out, and E brought his troops to join Chengsi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Dali, Xue Song of Xiang and Wei died. His younger brother E sought an acting commission, but the tooth general Pei Zhiqing drove him out. E brought his forces to Chengsi.

sentences.zh: 而帝自用李承昭為相州刺史，未至，承嗣使人訹吏士反，陽言救，實襲取之。

translations.literal: The emperor on his own authority appointed Li Chengzhao prefect of Xiang Prefecture; before he arrived, Chengsi incited officials and gentry to rebel, openly claiming to rescue them while in fact launching a surprise attack to seize the territory.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Li Chengzhao prefect of Xiang Prefecture on his own authority. Before Chengzhao arrived, Chengsi incited local officials and gentry to rebel, claiming to rescue them while in truth launching a surprise attack to seize the territory.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使者諭罷兵，承嗣不奉詔，遣將盧子期取洺州，楊光朝取衛州，脅刺史薛雄亂，不從，屠其家，悉四州兵財以歸，擅置守宰。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys ordering him to cease hostilities; Chengsi did not obey the edict. He dispatched generals Lu Ziqi to take Ming Prefecture and Yang Guangchao to take Wei Prefecture; he coerced the prefect Xue Xiong into rebellion, and when Xiong refused, slaughtered his household, gathered the troops and wealth of all four prefectures, and returned home, appointing governors and magistrates on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys ordering him to stand down; Chengsi ignored the edict. He sent Lu Ziqi to seize Ming Prefecture and Yang Guangchao to seize Wei Prefecture. He tried to coerce the prefect Xue Xiong into rebellion; when Xiong refused, Chengsi slaughtered his household, gathered the troops and wealth of all four prefectures, and returned home, appointing governors and magistrates at will.

sentences.zh: 逼使者行礠、相，遣劉渾從之，陰使從子悅諷諸將詣使者剺面請承嗣為帥，使人不敢詰，於是厚賞請己者。

translations.literal: He forced the envoy to proceed through Ci and Xiang; Liu Hun accompanied him, while secretly sending his nephew Yue to prompt the generals to go before the envoy and slash their faces, requesting Chengsi as commander. The envoy dared not question this, and Chengsi richly rewarded those who had petitioned for him.
translations.idiomatic: He forced the envoy to travel through Ci and Xiang, with Liu Hun escorting him, while secretly sending his nephew Yue to urge the generals to appear before the envoy with slashed faces, begging that Chengsi be made commander. The envoy dared not challenge them, and Chengsi richly rewarded those who had petitioned on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 帝乃下詔貶承嗣永州刺史，許一子從，悅及諸子皆逐惡地。

translations.literal: The emperor then issued an edict demoting Chengsi to prefect of Yong Prefecture, permitting one son to accompany him; Yue and the other sons were all exiled to harsh regions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then issued an edict demoting Chengsi to prefect of Yong Prefecture, allowing one son to accompany him. Yue and Chengsi's other sons were all exiled to remote and harsh lands.

sentences.zh: 詔河東節度使薛兼訓、成德李寶臣、幽州朱滔、昭義李承昭、淄青李正己、淮西李忠臣、永平李勉、汴宋田神玉等兵六萬掎角進，若承嗣不承命，聽在所討執，以軍法從事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Hedong military commissioner Xue Jianxun, Chengde's Li Baochen, Youzhou's Zhu Tao, Zhaoyi's Li Chengzhao, Ziqing's Li Zhengji, Huaixi's Li Zhongchen, Yongping's Li Mian, and Biansong's Tian Shenyu and others — six myriad troops advancing in pincer formation — that if Chengsi did not obey the command, each might attack and seize him wherever they encountered him, and deal with him by military law.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Hedong commissioner Xue Jianxun, Chengde's Li Baochen, Youzhou's Zhu Tao, Zhaoyi's Li Chengzhao, Ziqing's Li Zhengji, Huaixi's Li Zhongchen, Yongping's Li Mian, Biansong's Tian Shenyu, and others — sixty thousand troops advancing in concert — to attack and capture Chengsi wherever they met him if he refused the command, and to punish him by martial law.

sentences.zh: 其下霍榮國以礠降。

translations.literal: Below him, Huo Rongguo surrendered Ci Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Among his subordinates, Huo Rongguo surrendered Ci Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李正己攻拔德州，李忠臣攻衛，築偃月壁河上。

translations.literal: Li Zhengji captured and seized De Prefecture; Li Zhongchen attacked Wei and built a crescent fortification along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhengji captured De Prefecture; Li Zhongchen attacked Wei and built a crescent fortification along the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 承嗣列將往往攜阻，殺數十人乃定。

translations.literal: Chengsi's arrayed generals often wavered and obstructed; he killed several dozen men before order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi's deployed generals often faltered and obstructed one another; he executed several dozen men before restoring discipline.

sentences.zh: 帝又遣御史大夫李涵督諸節度並力。

translations.literal: The emperor also sent the censor-in-chief Li Han to supervise the military commissioners in combined action.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also dispatched Censor-in-Chief Li Han to supervise the commissioners in joint operations.

sentences.zh: 承嗣遣裴誌清等攻冀州，誌清以兵附成德，承嗣悉眾圍之，為寶臣所逐，火輜重，歸於貝，計益窮，不知所出，遣其下郝光朝奉表請委身北闕下。

translations.literal: Chengsi sent Pei Zhiqing and others to attack Ji Prefecture; Zhiqing attached his troops to Chengde; Chengsi mustered his entire force to besiege it, was driven off by Baochen, burned his baggage train, and returned to Bei; his plans grew ever more desperate and he knew not what to do; he sent his subordinate Hao Guangchao to submit a memorial asking to surrender himself at the northern gate of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi sent Pei Zhiqing and others to attack Ji Prefecture. Zhiqing attached his troops to Chengde. Chengsi mustered his entire army to besiege the city, was driven off by Baochen, burned his baggage train, and retreated to Bei. His options narrowed and he knew not what to do. He sent his subordinate Hao Guangchao to submit a memorial asking to surrender himself at the northern gate of the palace.

sentences.zh: 又使悅與盧子期將萬人攻礠州，屯東山。

translations.literal: He also sent Yue with Lu Ziqi and ten thousand men to attack Ci Prefecture, encamping at East Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Yue with Lu Ziqi and ten thousand men to attack Ci Prefecture, encamping at East Mountain.

sentences.zh: 宣慰使韓朝彩等固守，兼訓以萬騎屯西山，成德、幽州各遣兵救礠。

translations.literal: The pacification commissioner Han Chaocai and others held firm in defense; Jianxun encamped ten thousand cavalry on West Mountain; Chengde and Youzhou each sent troops to relieve Ci.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification commissioner Han Chaocai and others held firm in defense. Jianxun encamped ten thousand cavalry on West Mountain. Chengde and Youzhou each dispatched troops to relieve Ci.

sentences.zh: 時承昭以神策射生繼進，入河東壘。

translations.literal: At that time Chengzhao advanced in succession with the Shence Army's archers and entered the Hedong encampment.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chengzhao advanced in succession with the Shence Army's archers and entered the Hedong camp.

sentences.zh: 諸軍進討，數有功，頗賞，天子使中人多出禦服、良馬、黃白金萬計勞賚，使人供帳高會。

translations.literal: The allied armies pressed the attack and achieved several victories; rewards were generous; the Son of Heaven sent eunuchs bearing imperial garments, fine horses, and gold and white silver by the tens of thousands to bestow as rewards; envoys supplied pavilions and held grand feasts.
translations.idiomatic: The allied armies pressed the attack and won several victories. Rewards flowed freely. The emperor sent eunuchs bearing imperial garments, fine horses, and gold and silver by the tens of thousands. Envoys supplied pavilions and held grand feasts for the troops.

sentences.zh: 諸軍少懈，而正己、寶臣二軍會棗強，更相見。

translations.literal: The armies slackened somewhat; then the forces of Zhengji and Baochen met at Zaoqiang and exchanged visits.
translations.idiomatic: The armies slackened their pace. Then the forces of Zhengji and Baochen met at Zaoqiang and paid visits to one another.

sentences.zh: 會正己軍輒引去，忠臣乃棄月壘，濟河屯陽武。

translations.literal: When Zhengji's army abruptly withdrew, Zhongchen abandoned the crescent fortification, crossed the river, and encamped at Yangwu.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhengji's army suddenly withdrew, Zhongchen abandoned the crescent fortification, crossed the river, and encamped at Yangwu.

sentences.zh: 承昭使成德、幽州兵循東山襲子期軍，自閉壁以驕賊。

translations.literal: Chengzhao sent the Chengde and Youzhou troops along East Mountain to strike Ziqi's army, while he himself closed the walls to feign arrogance toward the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhao sent the Chengde and Youzhou troops along East Mountain to strike Ziqi's army, while he himself shut the gates and feigned contempt for the rebels.

sentences.zh: 子期分步騎萬人環承昭壁，以兵四千乘高望麾而進。

translations.literal: Ziqi divided infantry and cavalry — ten thousand men — to surround Chengzhao's walls, and with four thousand troops advanced from the heights at a signal.
translations.idiomatic: Ziqi divided ten thousand infantry and cavalry to surround Chengzhao's camp, then sent four thousand men from the heights to advance at his signal.

sentences.zh: 河東將劉文英、辛忠臣等決戰，而成德、幽州兵繞出子期後，於是圍解。

translations.literal: The Hedong generals Liu Wenying, Xin Zhongchen, and others joined battle; the Chengde and Youzhou troops circled out behind Ziqi — and so the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: The Hedong generals Liu Wenying, Xin Zhongchen, and others joined battle. The Chengde and Youzhou troops swung around behind Ziqi — and the siege was broken.

sentences.zh: 更陣高原，諸將與承昭夾攻，大戰臨水，賊敗，屍旁午數里，斬九千級、馬千匹，執子期及將士二千三百，旗纛器甲鼓角二十萬。

translations.literal: They re-formed on the high plain; the generals attacked in concert with Chengzhao; a great battle was fought by the water; the rebels were defeated; corpses lay crisscrossed for several li; nine thousand were beheaded, a thousand horses captured; Ziqi and two thousand three hundred officers and soldiers were taken; banners, armor, drums, and horns numbered two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: They re-formed on the high plain. The generals attacked in concert with Chengzhao. A great battle raged by the water. The rebels were routed. Corpses lay crisscrossed for miles. Nine thousand heads were taken, a thousand horses captured. Ziqi and two thousand three hundred officers and soldiers were seized, along with two hundred thousand banners, suits of armor, drums, and horns.

sentences.zh: 諸軍乘勝進，距礠十里，暮而舍。

translations.literal: The armies pressed their victory and advanced to within ten li of Ci; at dusk they encamped.
translations.idiomatic: The armies pressed their victory forward to within ten li of Ci and encamped at dusk.

sentences.zh: 承昭舉燧，朝彩出銳兵鼓噪薄魏營，斬首五百，悅驚，率餘兵夜走，盡棄旗幕鎧仗五千乘。

translations.literal: Chengzhao raised beacon fires; Chaocai sent crack troops with drums and shouts to press close on the Wei camp; five hundred heads were cut off; Yue was alarmed, led the remaining troops in flight by night, and abandoned five thousand cartloads of banners, tents, armor, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhao raised beacon fires. Chaocai sent crack troops with drums and battle cries to storm the Wei camp. Five hundred heads were taken. Yue, alarmed, fled by night with the survivors, abandoning five thousand cartloads of banners, tents, armor, and weapons.

sentences.zh: 成德將王武俊以子期歸寶臣，寶臣方攻洺州，因以示城下，降之，復徇瀛州，瀛州亦降。

translations.literal: The Chengde general Wang Wujun returned Ziqi to Baochen; Baochen was then attacking Ming Prefecture and displayed him below the walls to induce surrender; he then marched on Ying Prefecture, which also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The Chengde general Wang Wujun delivered Ziqi to Baochen. Baochen was then besieging Ming Prefecture and displayed Ziqi below the walls to compel surrender. He then marched on Ying Prefecture, which submitted as well.

sentences.zh: 得兵萬人，粟二十萬石，獻子期京師，斬之。

translations.literal: He gained ten thousand troops and two hundred thousand shi of grain; Ziqi was sent to the capital and executed.
translations.idiomatic: He gained ten thousand troops and two hundred thousand shi of grain. Ziqi was sent to the capital and executed.

sentences.zh: 天子遣中人勞寶臣，不為禮，寶臣乃貳，反攻朱滔，與承嗣和，承嗣與之滄州。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven sent a eunuch to reward Baochen, who did not observe proper ceremony; Baochen then turned disloyal, counterattacked Zhu Tao, made peace with Chengsi, and Chengsi gave him Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a eunuch to reward Baochen, who treated him without proper ceremony. Baochen then turned disloyal, counterattacked Zhu Tao, made peace with Chengsi, and Chengsi ceded Cang Prefecture to him.

sentences.zh: 正己又請天子許承嗣入朝。

translations.literal: Zhengji also asked the Son of Heaven to permit Chengsi to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengji also petitioned the emperor to allow Chengsi to come to court.

sentences.zh: 十一年，帝遣諫議大夫杜亞持節至魏受其降，許闔門還京師，赦魏博所管與更始。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, the emperor sent Remonstrance Officer Du Ya, bearing credentials, to Wei to accept his surrender, permitting him to return to the capital with his household, and granting amnesty to all under Weibo's jurisdiction as at the beginning of a new reign.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, the emperor sent Remonstrance Officer Du Ya, bearing imperial credentials, to Wei to accept his surrender — permitting him to return to the capital with his household and granting amnesty throughout Weibo's jurisdiction as at the dawn of a new reign.

sentences.zh: 承嗣逗留不至。

translations.literal: Chengsi lingered and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi lingered and never came.

sentences.zh: 其秋，復略滑州，敗李勉兵。

translations.literal: That autumn he again raided Hua Prefecture and defeated Li Mian's army.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he raided Hua Prefecture again and defeated Li Mian's army.

sentences.zh: 會李靈耀以汴州叛，詔忠臣、勉、河陽馬燧合討。

translations.literal: When Li Lingyao rebelled at Bian Prefecture, an edict ordered Zhongchen, Mian, and Heyang's Ma Sui to join in suppressing him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Lingyao rebelled at Bian Prefecture, an edict ordered Zhongchen, Mian, and Heyang's Ma Sui to join forces against him.

sentences.zh: 靈耀求救於魏，承嗣使悅將兵三萬赴之，敗勉將杜如江、正己將尹伯良，死者殆半，乘勝屯汴北郛，與靈耀合。

translations.literal: Lingyao sought rescue from Wei; Chengsi sent Yue with thirty thousand troops to his aid; they defeated Mian's general Du Rujiang and Zhengji's general Yin Boliang; nearly half the men died; pressing their victory they encamped at the northern outskirts of Bian and joined with Lingyao.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyao sought aid from Wei. Chengsi sent Yue with thirty thousand troops to his relief. They defeated Li Mian's general Du Rujiang and Li Zhengji's general Yin Boliang; nearly half their men fell. Pressing their victory, they encamped at the northern outskirts of Bian and joined Lingyao.

sentences.zh: 燧、忠臣逆擊，破之，悅脫身遁，斬獲數萬。

translations.literal: Sui and Zhongchen counterattacked and broke them; Yue escaped with his life; tens of thousands were killed or captured.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui and Zhongchen counterattacked and routed them. Yue escaped with his life. Tens of thousands were killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 靈耀東走，欲歸承嗣，為如江所禽，並魏將常準獻京師。

translations.literal: Lingyao fled east, wishing to return to Chengsi; he was captured by Rujiang, and together with the Wei general Chang Zhun was sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyao fled east, hoping to reach Chengsi. Du Rujiang captured him, and together with the Wei general Chang Zhun he was sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 明年，承嗣上書請罪，有詔復官爵，子弟皆仍故官，復賜鐵券。

translations.literal: The next year, Chengsi submitted a memorial begging forgiveness; an edict restored his offices and titles, his sons and brothers all retained their former posts, and iron tallies were granted again.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Tian Chengsi memorialized the throne to confess his crimes. An edict restored his titles and offices, his sons and brothers were all returned to their former posts, and he was once again granted an iron certificate of immunity.

sentences.zh: 承嗣盜有貝、搏、魏、衛、相、礠、洺七州，而未嘗北面天子。

translations.literal: Chengsi illicitly held Bei, Bo, Wei, Weizhou, Xiang, Ci, and Ming—seven prefectures—and yet never once faced north toward the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi held seven prefectures by force—Bei, Bo, Wei, Weizhou, Xiang, Ci, and Ming—and yet never once turned north in submission to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 凡再興師，會國威中奪，窮而復縱，故承嗣得肆奸無怖忌。

translations.literal: In all he raised armies twice; each time when the state's prestige was at its height he was stripped of power, but when cornered he was released again, so Chengsi was able to indulge in treachery without fear or restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Twice the court raised armies against him; twice, when imperial authority was at its peak, he was brought low—only to be pardoned when desperate. Thus Chengsi grew bold in his wickedness, without fear or restraint.

sentences.zh: 十四年死，年七十五，贈太保。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died, aged seventy-five; he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourteenth year, at the age of seventy-five, and was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 悅，蚤孤，母更嫁平盧戍卒，悅隨母轉側淄、青間。

translations.literal: Yue was orphaned early; his mother remarried a Pinglu garrison soldier, and Yue wandered with his mother between Zi and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Yue lost his father while still young. His mother remarried a soldier of the Pinglu garrison, and Yue drifted with her between Zi and Qing.

sentences.zh: 承嗣得魏，訪獲之，年十三，拜伏有禮，承嗣異之，委以號令，裁處皆與承嗣意合。

translations.literal: When Chengsi took Wei, he found Yue through search; Yue was thirteen. He bowed with propriety, and Chengsi thought him unusual. Chengsi entrusted him with commands, and his decisions all accorded with Chengsi's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengsi secured Wei, he tracked Yue down. The boy was thirteen. He prostrated himself with perfect courtesy, and Chengsi, struck by the lad, put him in charge of issuing orders. Every decision Yue made matched Chengsi's own wishes.

sentences.zh: 及長，剽悍善鬥冠軍中，賊忍狙詐，外飭行義，輕財重施，以鉤美譽，人皆附之。

translations.literal: When grown, he was fierce and excelled in fighting, foremost in the army; treacherous, cruel, and cunning, outwardly he cultivated righteousness, lightly valued wealth and heavily gave gifts to hook good reputation, and all attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew to manhood he became the fiercest fighter in the army—ruthless, cunning, and deceitful by nature, yet outwardly devoted to propriety. He spent freely and gave generously to win a fine reputation, and men flocked to his side.

sentences.zh: 承嗣愛其才，將死，顧諸子弱，乃命悅知節度事，令諸子佐之。

translations.literal: Chengshi admired his talent. On the point of death, seeing his sons were weak, he ordered Yue to manage the frontier command and had his sons assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi admired his ability. Near death, seeing his own sons too weak to govern, he put Yue in charge of the command and ordered his sons to assist him.

sentences.zh: 帝因詔悅自中軍兵馬使、府左司馬擢留後，俄檢校工部尚書，為節度使。

translations.literal: The Emperor accordingly issued an edict promoting Yue from Central Army Military Commissioner and Left Assistant of the prefectural staff to acting military governor; soon he was made inspecting Minister of Works and military governor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then promoted Yue from Central Army Military Commissioner and Left Assistant of the prefectural staff to acting military governor. Before long he was made inspecting Minister of Works and confirmed as military governor.

sentences.zh: 悅始招致賢才，開館宇，禮天下士，外示恭順，陰濟其奸。

translations.literal: Yue began to recruit talented men, opened halls, treated scholars of the realm with courtesy, outwardly showed submission, and secretly facilitated his treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Yue began recruiting men of talent, opened guest halls, and treated scholars from across the realm with honor. Outwardly he appeared dutiful and obedient; in secret he furthered his treacherous designs.

sentences.zh: 帝晚年尤寬弛，悅所奏請無不從。

translations.literal: In his later years the Emperor was especially lenient and slack; whatever Yue memorialized was never denied.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the emperor grew especially indulgent and lax. Nothing Yue requested was ever refused.

sentences.zh: 德宗立，不假借方鎮，諸將稍惕息。

translations.literal: When Dezong ascended the throne, he did not indulge the regional commands, and the various generals gradually grew wary and subdued.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong took the throne, he showed no indulgence toward the regional commands, and the generals gradually grew cautious and subdued.

sentences.zh: 會黜陟使洪經綸至河北，聞悅養士七萬，輒下符罷其四萬歸田畝。

translations.literal: It happened that the appointment-and-dismissal commissioner Hong Jinglun arrived in Hebei; hearing that Yue maintained seventy thousand soldiers, he immediately issued orders dismissing forty thousand to return to farming.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the appointment-and-dismissal commissioner Hong Jinglun reached Hebei. Learning that Yue maintained an army of seventy thousand men, he immediately issued orders dismissing forty thousand of them to return to the fields.

sentences.zh: 悅即奉命，因大集將士，以好言激之曰：「而等籍軍中久，仰縑廩養父母妻子，今罷去，何恃而生？」

translations.literal: Yue immediately obeyed the order. Thereupon he greatly assembled officers and soldiers and, using kind words to stir them, said: You all have long been registered in the army, relying on silk and grain rations to support your parents, wives, and children. Now dismissed, on what will you depend to live?
translations.idiomatic: Yue at once accepted the order. Then he gathered all his officers and soldiers and roused them with gentle words: You have served in the army for years, depending on silk and grain rations to feed your parents, wives, and children. If you are dismissed now, how will you live?

sentences.zh: 眾大哭。

translations.literal: The whole crowd wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: The men broke into loud weeping.

sentences.zh: 悅乃悉出家貲給之，各令還部，自此，魏人德悅。

translations.literal: Yue then gave all of his personal wealth to them and ordered each to return to his unit. From this the people of Wei were grateful to Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Yue then distributed his entire personal fortune among them and sent each man back to his unit. From that day the people of Wei regarded Yue with gratitude.

sentences.zh: 及劉晏死，藩帥益懼，又傳言帝且東封泰山，李勉遂城汴州；

translations.literal: When Liu Yan died, the frontier governors grew more fearful. There was also a rumor that the Emperor would soon conduct the eastern feng at Mount Tai, and Li Mian then fortified Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yan's death the military governors grew still more fearful. Rumors spread that the emperor would soon perform the eastern feng rite at Mount Tai, and Li Mian hastily fortified Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 而李正己懼，率兵萬人屯曹州，乃遣人說悅同叛。

translations.literal: Li Zhengji was fearful; he led ten thousand troops and encamped at Caozhou, then sent men to persuade Yue to rebel together.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhengji, seized with fear, led ten thousand men to encamp at Caozhou and sent envoys to urge Yue to join him in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 悅因與梁崇義等阻兵連和，以王侑、扈、許士則為腹心；

translations.literal: Yue thus joined with Liang Chongyi and others in blocking with troops and forming alliances, making Wang You, Hu, and Xu Shize his inner circle.
translations.idiomatic: Yue accordingly joined Liang Chongyi and others in raising troops and forming alliances. Wang You, Hu, and Xu Shize became his closest confidants.

sentences.zh: 邢曹俊、孟希祐、李長春、符璘、康愔為爪牙。

translations.literal: Xing Caojun, Meng Xiyou, Li Changchun, Fu Lin, and Kang Yin served as his claws and teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Caojun, Meng Xiyou, Li Changchun, Fu Lin, and Kang Yin served as his chief enforcers.

sentences.zh: 建中二年，鎮州李惟嶽、淄青李納求襲節度，不許，悅為請，不答，遂合謀同叛。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianzhong, Zhenzhou's Li Weiyue and Ziqing's Li Na sought to inherit their fathers' commands and were not permitted. Yue pleaded on their behalf and received no answer, so they conspired together to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianzhong, Li Weiyue of Zhenzhou and Li Na of Ziqing petitioned to succeed their fathers as military governors and were refused. Yue interceded for them but received no reply, and the three men then plotted rebellion together.

sentences.zh: 會於邵、令狐亙等表汰浮圖，悅乃詐其軍曰：「有詔閱軍之老疾疲弱者。」

translations.literal: It happened that Yu Shao, Linghu Geng, and others memorialized to reduce Buddhist temples. Yue then deceived his army, saying: There is an edict to review the army's old, sick, weak, and feeble.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yu Shao, Linghu Geng, and others submitted a memorial calling for the reduction of Buddhist temples. Yue then deceived his troops, saying: An edict has come to inspect the army and dismiss the old, sick, weak, and infirm.

sentences.zh: 繇是舉軍咨怨。

translations.literal: From this the whole army grumbled with resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The entire army erupted in angry complaint.

sentences.zh: 悅與納會濮陽，納分兵佐悅。

translations.literal: Yue met Na at Puyang, and Na divided troops to assist Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Yue met with Li Na at Puyang, and Na detached part of his force to support him.

sentences.zh: 會幽州朱滔等奉詔討惟嶽，悅乃遣孟希祐以兵五千助惟嶽；

translations.literal: It happened that Zhu Tao of Youzhou and others received orders to attack Weiyue. Yue then sent Meng Xiyou with five thousand troops to assist Weiyue.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Zhu Tao of Youzhou and others had received orders to campaign against Li Weiyue. Yue sent Meng Xiyou with five thousand men to aid Weiyue.

sentences.zh: 別遣康愔以兵八千攻邢州；

translations.literal: Separately he sent Kang Yin with eight thousand troops to attack Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time he dispatched Kang Yin with eight thousand men to attack Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 楊朝光以兵五千壁盧疃，絕昭義餉道。

translations.literal: Yang Chaoguang, with five thousand troops, fortified Lu Tuan and cut off the Zhaoyi supply route.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chaoguang encamped at Lu Tuan with five thousand men and severed the Zhaoyi army's supply line.

sentences.zh: 悅自將兵數萬繼進，又使朝光攻臨洺將張伾。

translations.literal: Yue personally led tens of thousands of troops in continued advance, and also had Chaoguang attack Linming's commander Zhang Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Yue himself led several tens of thousands of men in pursuit, and ordered Chaoguang to press the attack against Zhang Pei, the Linming commander.

sentences.zh: 伾固守，食且盡，賞賜不足，乃飾愛女示眾曰：「庫廩竭矣，願以此女代賞。」

translations.literal: Pei defended steadfastly; food was nearly exhausted and rewards were insufficient. He then adorned his beloved daughter and showed her to the troops, saying: The storehouses are depleted; I wish to offer this daughter in place of reward.
translations.idiomatic: Pei held firm, but provisions were nearly gone and he had nothing left with which to reward his men. He dressed his beloved daughter in finery and presented her to the army, saying: Our granaries are empty. Let this girl stand in place of the bounty you deserve.

sentences.zh: 士感泣，請死戰，大破悅軍。

translations.literal: The soldiers were moved to tears and asked to fight to the death; they greatly defeated Yue's army.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers wept at the sight and begged to fight to the death. They routed Yue's army.

sentences.zh: 有詔河東馬燧、河陽李芃與昭義軍救伾。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Hedong's Ma Sui, Heyang's Li Pi, and the Zhaoyi army to rescue Pei.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict ordered Ma Sui of Hedong, Li Pi of Heyang, and the Zhaoyi army to relieve Zhang Pei.

sentences.zh: 三節度次狗、明二山間，未進。

translations.literal: The three commanders halted between the Gou and Ming mountains and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The three commanders encamped between Mount Gou and Mount Ming and made no move forward.

sentences.zh: 伾急，以紙為風鳶，高百餘丈，過悅營上，悅使善射者射之，不能及。

translations.literal: Pei was desperate; he made a paper kite over a hundred zhang high. It passed above Yue's camp. Yue sent skilled archers to shoot it down, but they could not reach it.
translations.idiomatic: In desperation Pei fashioned a paper kite more than a hundred zhang high and sent it drifting over Yue's camp. Yue ordered his best archers to bring it down, but none could reach it.

sentences.zh: 燧營噪迎之，得書言「三日不解，臨洺士且為悅食。」

translations.literal: Ma Sui's camp clamored to receive it and obtained the letter, which read: If not relieved within three days, the soldiers of Linming will become Yue's food.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui's camp erupted in shouts as the kite was retrieved. The message inside read: If we are not relieved within three days, the men of Linming will be eaten by Yue's troops.

sentences.zh: 燧乃自壺關鼓而東，破盧疃，戰雙岡，禽賊大將盧子昌而殺朝光，悅遁保洹水。

translations.literal: Ma Sui then beat drums eastward from Huguan, broke Lu Tuan, fought at Shuang'gang, captured the rebel general Lu Zichang and killed Chaoguang. Yue fled and defended the Huan River.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui then marched east from Huguan to the beat of drums, smashed Lu Tuan, fought at Shuang'gang, captured the rebel general Lu Zichang, and killed Yang Chaoguang. Yue fled and took refuge behind the Huan River.

sentences.zh: 於是曹俊為貝州刺史，乃承嗣時舊將，果而謀。

translations.literal: At this time Caojun was prefect of Beizhou; he was a former general from Chengsi's time, decisive and scheming.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Xing Caojun was prefect of Beizhou—a veteran general from Chengsi's day, bold in counsel and shrewd in design.

sentences.zh: 悅未得誌，召問計安出，對曰：「兵法，十則攻，今公以逆幹順，勢不敵也。

translations.literal: Yue had not achieved his aim and summoned Caojun, asking where a plan might come from. Caojun replied: In the art of war, attack only when you have tenfold strength. Now you oppose loyalty with rebellion; the odds cannot match.
translations.idiomatic: Frustrated in his ambitions, Yue summoned Caojun and asked what course he should take. Caojun answered: The art of war teaches that one attacks only with tenfold strength. You now meet loyal forces with rebellion—the balance of power is against you.

sentences.zh: 宜留兵萬人屯崞阝口，以遏西師，則舉河北二十四州，惟公所命。

translations.literal: You should leave ten thousand troops garrisoned at Guokou to block the western army; then all twenty-four prefectures of Hebei would be yours to command.
translations.idiomatic: Leave ten thousand men at Guokou to hold the western armies at bay, and all twenty-four prefectures of Hebei will lie at your command.

sentences.zh: 今攻臨洺，糧竭卒老，不見其可。」

translations.literal: To attack Linming now, with grain exhausted and soldiers worn, I see no possibility of success.
translations.idiomatic: To press the siege of Linming now, with provisions spent and troops exhausted, is a course I cannot see succeeding.

sentences.zh: 悅所昵扈、孟希祐等皆訾短之，故悅不聽其言。

translations.literal: Yue's favorites Hu, Meng Xiyou, and the others all belittled him, so Yue did not heed his words.
translations.idiomatic: Hu, Meng Xiyou, and the other men Yue favored all spoke against Caojun, and Yue refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 燧等距悅軍三十里，築壘相望。

translations.literal: Ma Sui and the others were thirty li from Yue's army and built ramparts facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui and his allies halted thirty li from Yue's force and built opposing fortifications.

sentences.zh: 悅與納合兵三萬，陣洹水。

translations.literal: Yue and Na joined forces—thirty thousand men—and formed battle lines at the Huan River.
translations.idiomatic: Yue and Li Na combined their armies—thirty thousand strong—and drew up battle lines along the Huan River.

sentences.zh: 燧引神策將李晟夾攻悅，悅大敗，死傷二萬計，引壯騎數十夜奔魏，其將李長春拒關不內，以須官軍。

translations.literal: Ma Sui led the Shence general Li Sheng in a pincer attack on Yue. Yue was greatly defeated; dead and wounded totaled twenty thousand. He fled by night to Wei with several tens of elite cavalry. His general Li Changchun barred the pass and would not admit him, intending to wait for the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui brought the Shence general Li Sheng to attack Yue from both flanks. Yue suffered a crushing defeat, with some twenty thousand dead and wounded. He fled by night toward Wei with a few dozen picked horsemen. His general Li Changchun closed the pass and refused him entry, hoping to hold out for the imperial forces.

sentences.zh: 而三帥頓不進。

translations.literal: But the three commanders halted and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the three commanders held their positions and did not press forward.

sentences.zh: 明日，悅得入，殺長春，持佩刀立軍門，流涕曰：「悅藉伯父餘業，與君等同休戚。

translations.literal: The next day Yue gained entry, killed Changchun, and, holding his sword, stood at the army gate weeping. He said: Yue relies on my uncle's remaining enterprise and shares weal and woe with you all alike.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yue gained entry and killed Changchun. Sword in hand, he stood before the army gate in tears and said: I inherited my uncle's legacy and have shared fortune and misfortune with you all.

sentences.zh: 今敗亡及此，不敢圖全。

translations.literal: Now defeat and ruin have reached this point; I dare not seek to preserve myself.
translations.idiomatic: Now defeat has brought us to this pass, and I no longer dare hope for survival.

sentences.zh: 然悅久稽天誅者，特以淄青、恒冀子弟不得承襲，既弗能報，乃至用兵，使士民塗炭。

translations.literal: Yet the reason Yue long delayed Heaven's punishment was only that the sons of Ziqing and Hengji could not inherit their commands. Unable to repay that debt, I resorted to arms and brought suffering upon soldiers and people alike.
translations.idiomatic: The reason I have long evaded Heaven's judgment is simply this: the heirs of Ziqing and Hengji were denied their rightful succession. Unable to make amends by any other means, I took up arms and brought ruin upon soldiers and civilians alike.

sentences.zh: 悅正緣母老不能自剄，願公等斬悅首以取富貴，無庸俱死。」

translations.literal: Yue, only because my mother is old, cannot cut my own throat. I wish you all to behead me and win wealth and honor; there is no need for all of us to die together.
translations.idiomatic: Only because my mother is old do I lack the courage to fall on my own sword. Cut off my head and claim your reward—there is no need for you all to perish with me.

sentences.zh: 乃自投於地。

translations.literal: Then he threw himself to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: With that he cast himself to the ground.

sentences.zh: 眾憐，皆抱持之曰：「今士馬之眾，尚可一戰，事脫不濟，死生以之。」

translations.literal: The crowd pitied him; all embraced and held him, saying: Our troops and horses are still numerous and can fight one more battle. If matters by chance do not succeed, then life or death be as it may.
translations.idiomatic: The men were moved to pity and gathered around him, saying: Our force is still strong enough for one more fight. If fortune fails us, then so be it—we live or die together.

sentences.zh: 悅收淚曰：「諸公不以悅喪敗，誓同存亡，縱身先地下，敢忘厚意乎？」

translations.literal: Yue wiped away tears and said: You gentlemen do not treat Yue as ruined in defeat; you swear to live and die together. Even if I go first to the underworld, how could I dare forget such deep kindness?
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue wiped away his tears and said, You do not hold my defeat against me—you have sworn to stand or fall together. Even if I die first, how could I ever forget such loyalty?

sentences.zh: 乃斷發為誓，將士亦斷發，約為兄弟；

translations.literal: Then he cut off his hair as an oath; the officers and soldiers also cut off their hair, pledging to become brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He then cut his hair to seal the oath, and his officers and men did the same, binding themselves as sworn brothers.

sentences.zh: 乃率富民大家財及府庫所有，大行賜與。

translations.literal: Then he gathered the wealth of rich households and great families, together with everything in the treasury, and distributed rewards on a grand scale.
translations.idiomatic: He then pooled the riches of wealthy families and the entire contents of the treasury and distributed them lavishly among his men.

sentences.zh: 而李再春及其子瑤以博州降，悅從兄昂以洺州降，燧等受之、悅皆族昂等家。

translations.literal: But Li Zaichun and his son Yao surrendered Bozhou; Yue's cousin Ang surrendered Mingzhou; Sui and the others accepted them—and Yue executed all the families of Ang and the others to the last clan member.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zaichun and his son Yao surrendered Bozhou, and Yue's cousin Ang surrendered Mingzhou; though Ma Sui and the others accepted their surrender, Yue had Ang's entire family—and those of the others—put to death.

sentences.zh: 悅自視兵械乏，眾單耗，懼，不知所出，復召曹俊與之謀。

translations.literal: Yue saw for himself that weapons were scarce and his forces few and depleted; afraid and not knowing what course to take, he again summoned Cao Jun to consult with him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his arms exhausted and his ranks thinned, Tian Yue grew fearful and at a loss. He summoned Cao Jun once more to counsel him.

sentences.zh: 曹俊為整軍完壘以振士氣，群心復堅，後十餘日，燧等始進薄城下。

translations.literal: Cao Jun reorganized the army and completed the fortifications to raise morale; the hearts of the masses again hardened. More than ten days later, Sui and the others began advancing to press close beneath the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jun drilled the troops and strengthened the ramparts to restore morale, and their resolve firmed again. More than ten days passed before Ma Sui and his allies at last pressed up to the walls.

sentences.zh: 未幾，王武俊殺惟嶽，而深州降朱滔，滔分兵守之。

translations.literal: Before long, Wang Wujun killed Wei Yue, and Shenzhou surrendered to Zhu Tao; Tao divided troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wang Wujun killed Li Weiyue, Shenzhou submitted to Zhu Tao, and Tao posted troops to hold it.

sentences.zh: 天子授武俊恒州刺史，以康日知為深、趙二州觀察使。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven appointed Wujun governor of Hengzhou and made Kang Rizhi military commissioner of Shen and Zhao prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Wang Wujun governor of Hengzhou and made Kang Rizhi military commissioner over Shen and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 武俊恨賞薄，滔怨不得深州，悅知二將可間，乃路使王侑、許士則說滔曰：「司徒奉詔討賊，不十日，拔束鹿，下深州，惟嶽勢蹙，故王大夫能得逆首。

translations.literal: Wujun resented the meager rewards; Tao resented not obtaining Shenzhou. Yue knew the two generals could be estranged, so he bribed and sent Wang You and Xu Shize to persuade Tao, saying: The Minister of Works received the edict to suppress rebels; in less than ten days he took Shulu and captured Shenzhou. Wei Yue's position was desperate, so Lord Wang was able to obtain the rebel's head.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujun resented his stingy reward; Zhu Tao resented losing Shenzhou. Tian Yue saw that the two could be set against each other, and sent Wang You and Xu Shize with bribes to win Tao over. They said, Your Excellency received the imperial command to suppress rebellion. In fewer than ten days you took Shulu and seized Shenzhou. Li Weiyue was cornered—that is how Lord Wang won the rebel's head.

sentences.zh: 聞出幽州日，有詔破惟嶽得其地即隸麾下，今乃以深州與康日知，是朝廷不信於公也。

translations.literal: It is heard that on the day you left Youzhou, there was an edict that whoever defeated Wei Yue and took his territory would have it placed under his command. Yet now Shenzhou has been given to Kang Rizhi—this means the court does not trust you.
translations.idiomatic: When you marched out of Youzhou, we hear, the throne decreed that whoever broke Li Weiyue and took his lands would keep them under his own command. Now Shenzhou has been handed to Kang Rizhi. The court plainly does not trust you.

sentences.zh: 且上英武獨斷，有秦皇、漢武風，將誅豪桀，掃除河朔，不使父子相襲。

translations.literal: Moreover, the emperor is heroic and resolute, with the spirit of Qin Shihuang and Emperor Wu of Han; he intends to execute powerful magnates, sweep clean the lands north of the Yellow River, and not allow offices to pass from father to son.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the Son of Heaven is bold and decisive—he has something of the First Emperor and Han Wudi in him. He means to destroy the great warlords of the north, purge the Hebei provinces, and end hereditary rule.

sentences.zh: 又功臣劉晏等皆旋踵破滅，殺梁崇義，誅其口三百餘，血丹漢江。

translations.literal: Again, meritorious ministers like Liu Yan were destroyed in the turning of a heel; Liang Chongyi was killed, and more than three hundred of his kin were executed—the Han River ran red with blood.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious ministers such as Liu Yan were ruined almost overnight. Liang Chongyi was slain, and more than three hundred members of his clan were executed until the Han River ran red.

sentences.zh: 今日破魏，則取燕、趙如牽轅下馬耳。

translations.literal: If Wei is taken today, seizing Yan and Zhao will be like leading a horse down from under the axle—effortless.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wei falls, taking Yan and Zhao will be as easy as leading a horse down from beneath the axle.

sentences.zh: 夫魏博全則燕、趙安，鄙州尚書必以死報德。

translations.literal: When Weibo is intact, Yan and Zhao are secure; this humble prefecture's minister will surely repay your grace with his life.
translations.idiomatic: While Weibo stands whole, Yan and Zhao remain safe. Your humble servant will repay your kindness with his life.

sentences.zh: 且合從連衡，救災恤患，不朽之業也，尚書願上貝州以廣湯沐，使侑等奉簿最孔目，司徒朝至魏則夕入貝，惟孰計之。」

translations.literal: Moreover, alliance through united fronts and mutual pacts, saving one another in calamity and sharing in distress—that is an immortal achievement. The minister is willing to offer up Beizhou to enlarge your fief; let You and the others present the ledgers and accounts. If the Minister of Works reaches Wei in the morning, he will enter Bei by evening—pray consider this.
translations.idiomatic: To league together in alliance, to succor one another in disaster—that is work that outlasts a lifetime. Your servant is willing to surrender Beizhou to enlarge your domain. Let Wang You and the others bring the registers and tallies. If Your Excellency reaches Wei by morning, you may enter Bei by evening. We beg you to weigh this carefully.

sentences.zh: 滔心素欲得貝，即大喜，使侑先還告師期。

translations.literal: Tao had long desired Beizhou; he was greatly pleased and sent You back first to announce the date for mobilization.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao had long coveted Beizhou. Overjoyed, he sent Wang You back at once to set the date for marching.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔武俊出恒冀粟三十萬賜滔，使還幽州，以突騎五百助燧軍。

translations.literal: Previously, an edict ordered Wujun to provide three hundred thousand bushels of grain from Heng and Ji to bestow on Tao, return to Youzhou, and send five hundred crack cavalry to assist Sui's army.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the throne had ordered Wang Wujun to furnish three hundred thousand bushels of grain from Heng and Ji for Zhu Tao, return to Youzhou, and detach five hundred mounted shock troops to reinforce Ma Sui.

sentences.zh: 武俊懼悅破，將起師北伐，不肯歸粟、馬。

translations.literal: Wujun feared Yue would be defeated and planned to raise his army for a northern campaign; he refused to return the grain and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujun feared that Tian Yue would be destroyed and intended to march north himself. He refused to surrender the grain or the horses.

sentences.zh: 滔因使王郅說武俊曰：「天子以君善戰，天下無前，故分散粟、馬以弱君軍。

translations.literal: Tao thereupon sent Wang Zhi to persuade Wujun, saying: The Son of Heaven, because you are skilled in battle and unmatched under heaven, deliberately dispersed your grain and horses to weaken your army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao then sent Wang Zhi to persuade him. The Son of Heaven knows you are the finest fighter under heaven, he said. That is why he scattered your grain and horses—to weaken your army.

sentences.zh: 今若舉魏博，則王師北向，漳、滏勢危。

translations.literal: If Weibo is taken now, the imperial armies will turn north; Zhang and Fu will be in peril.
translations.idiomatic: If Weibo falls now, the imperial armies will wheel north, and Zhang and Fu will be in grave danger.

sentences.zh: 誠能連營南旆，解田悅於倒縣，大夫之利也，豈特粟不出窖，馬不離廄，又有排危之義，聲滿天下。

translations.literal: If you truly could link camps and march south with banners unfurled, relieving Tian Yue from his hanging peril—that would be to the lord's advantage. Would it not only mean grain staying in the granary and horses never leaving the stable, but also the renown of rescuing one in danger would resound throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: If you truly joined camps and marched south under your banners, lifting Tian Yue from his desperate plight, that would serve my lord well. Not only would your grain remain in the storehouse and your horses in the stable—you would also win the fame of saving a man in peril, and your name would fill the realm.

sentences.zh: 大夫親斷逆首，血蔑釁衣袖，日知不出趙城，何功於國，而坐兼二州。

translations.literal: The lord personally severed the rebel head; blood stained your sleeves at the oath-taking. Rizhi never left Zhao city—what service did he render the state, yet he sits holding two prefectures?
translations.idiomatic: My lord cut off the rebel's head himself—his blood stained your sleeve when you swore your oath. Kang Rizhi never even left Zhao city. What deed did he perform for the empire, that he should sit holding two prefectures?

sentences.zh: 河北士以不得深州為大夫恥。」

translations.literal: The gentlemen of Hebei take it as a shame to the lord that he did not obtain Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Every man of Hebei counts it a disgrace to my lord that he was denied Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 武俊既得深，亦喜，即日使使報滔。

translations.literal: Wujun, having already obtained what he wanted regarding Shen, was also pleased and that very day sent envoys to report to Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujun, now satisfied on the matter of Shenzhou, was pleased as well, and that same day sent envoys to inform Zhu Tao.

sentences.zh: 於是滔率兵二萬屯寧晉，武俊以兵萬五千會之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Tao led twenty thousand troops to encamp at Ningjin; Wujun joined him with fifteen thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao then led twenty thousand men to encamp at Ningjin, and Wang Wujun joined him with fifteen thousand.

sentences.zh: 悅恃救至，使康愔督兵與王師戰禦河上，大敗，棄甲走城。

translations.literal: Yue, relying on rescue having arrived, sent Kang Yin to command troops to fight the imperial army defending along the river; they were utterly defeated, cast off their armor, and fled toward the city.
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened by the arrival of relief, Tian Yue sent Kang Yin to lead his troops against the imperial forces on the riverbank. They were routed, threw off their armor, and fled back toward the city.

sentences.zh: 悅怒，閉門不內，蹈藉死塹中者甚眾。

translations.literal: Yue was enraged, closed the gates and would not admit them; many were trampled to death in the moat.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue flew into a rage, shut the gates, and refused them entry. Many were trampled to death in the moat.

sentences.zh: 其夏，滔、武俊軍至，悅具牛酒迎犒。

translations.literal: That summer, when Tao's and Wujun's armies arrived, Yue prepared cattle and wine to welcome and reward them.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, when the armies of Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun arrived, Tian Yue laid out oxen and wine to welcome and feast them.

sentences.zh: 燧等營魏河西，武俊、滔、悅壁河東，起樓櫓營中，兩軍相持，自秋汔冬。

translations.literal: Sui and the others camped west of the Wei River; Wujun, Tao, and Yue fortified east of the river, building watchtowers and ramparts in their camps. The two armies faced off from autumn until winter's end.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui and his allies encamped west of the Wei River; Wang Wujun, Zhu Tao, and Tian Yue fortified the east bank, raising watchtowers and palisades in their camps. The two sides faced each other from autumn through winter.

sentences.zh: 燧遣晟以兵三千，自邢、趙與張孝忠合攻涿、莫二州，以絕幽、薊路。

translations.literal: Sui sent Li Sheng with three thousand troops from Xing and Zhao to join Zhang Xiaozhong in attacking Zhuo and Mo prefectures, to cut off the route to You and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui dispatched Li Sheng with three thousand men from Xing and Zhao to join Zhang Xiaozhong in assailing Zhuo and Mo, severing the road to You and Ji.

sentences.zh: 悅重德滔，欲推為盟主而臣之。

translations.literal: Yue held Tao in high esteem and wished to make him alliance leader and submit to him as lord.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue held Zhu Tao in deep respect and wished to make him leader of the alliance and submit to him as sovereign.

sentences.zh: 滔不敢當，乃更議如七國故事。

translations.literal: Tao dared not accept; they then reconsidered following the precedent of the Seven Warring States.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao declined the honor, and they settled instead on the old arrangement of the Seven Warring States.

sentences.zh: 悅國號魏，僭稱魏王，以府為大名府，署子為府留後；

translations.literal: Yue took the state name Wei, arrogated the title King of Wei, made his headquarters Daming Prefecture, and appointed his son as acting prefect of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue declared his state Wei, took the title King of Wei, made Daming his capital, and appointed his son acting prefect of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以扈為留守，許士則為司武，曾穆司文，裴抗司禮，封演司刑，並為侍郎；

translations.literal: He made Hu garrison commander; Xu Shize Minister of War; Zeng Mu Minister of Rites for documents; Pei Kang Minister of Rites for ceremonies; Feng Yan Minister of Punishment—all as vice-ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Hu as garrison commander; Xu Shize as Minister of War; Zeng Mu as Minister of Documents; Pei Kang as Minister of Rites; and Feng Yan as Minister of Punishment—all with the rank of vice minister.

sentences.zh: 劉士素為內史舍人，張瑜、孫光佐為給事中，邢曹俊、孟希祐為左右仆射，田晁、高緬為征西節度使，蔡濟、薛有倫為虎牙將軍，高崇節知軍前兵馬，夏侯<赤真>為兵馬使。

translations.literal: Liu Shisu as Palace Secretariat attendant; Zhang Yu and Sun Guangzuo as supervisory censors; Xing Caojun and Meng Xiyou as Left and Right Vice Premiers; Tian Chao and Gao Mian as military commissioners of the Western Expedition; Cai Ji and Xue Youlun as Tigertooth Generals; Gao Chongjie in charge of front-line horse and foot; Xiahou Chizhen as army horse commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shisu became Secretariat Attendant; Zhang Yu and Sun Guangzuo, Supervising Censors; Xing Caojun and Meng Xiyou, Left and Right Vice Premiers; Tian Chao and Gao Mian, Commissioners of the Western Expedition; Cai Ji and Xue Youlun, Tigertooth Generals; Gao Chongjie, commander of the vanguard; and Xiahou Chizhen, Army Horse Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 晁以兵數千助李納守鄆。

translations.literal: Chao led several thousand troops to assist Li Na in defending Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chao led several thousand men to help Li Na hold Yan.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，滔屯河間，留大將馬寔以兵萬人戍魏。

translations.literal: The next summer, Tao encamped at Hejian, leaving his great general Ma Shi with ten thousand troops to garrison Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The following summer Zhu Tao encamped at Hejian and left his chief general Ma Shi with ten thousand men to guard Wei.

sentences.zh: 會朱泚亂，帝出奉天，燧還太原，武俊等皆罷，悅餞之，厚遺武俊、寔，官屬皆有贈。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci's rebellion broke out, the emperor went out to Fengtian; Sui returned to Taiyuan; Wujun and the others all withdrew. Yue saw them off with a farewell feast, lavishly gifting Wujun and Shi; every official received presents.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled and the emperor withdrew to Fengtian, Ma Sui returned to Taiyuan and Wang Wujun and the others broke off the siege. Tian Yue gave them a lavish farewell, heaping gifts on Wang Wujun and Ma Shi and presenting every officer with parting rewards.

sentences.zh: 興元元年，滔自將兵欲南度河助泚，使王郅見悅計事曰：「頃大王在重圍，孤與趙刻日赴王難以全魏、貝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan, Tao personally led his army intending to cross the river south to aid Ci; he sent Wang Zhi to see Yue and discuss affairs, saying: Recently when the Great King was in heavy siege, I and Zhao set a date and rushed to your distress to preserve Wei and Bei.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xingyuan reign, Zhu Tao personally led his army south intending to cross the river and aid Zhu Ci. He sent Wang Zhi to consult with Tian Yue. When Your Majesty was hemmed in tight, he said, Zhao and I fixed a day and raced to your rescue to preserve Wei and Bei.

sentences.zh: 今秦帝已據關中，孤以步騎十萬與回紇趨東都相應接，王能從孤濟河，合勢以取大梁，孤得西收鞏、陜，與秦兵會，天下可定也。

translations.literal: Now the Qin Emperor has already occupied Guanzhong; I shall lead one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry with the Uyghurs in a dash toward the eastern capital to coordinate. If the King can cross the river with me, combining forces to take Daliang—I can then turn west to seize Gong and Shaan and join the Qin armies—the realm can be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Emperor of Qin holds Guanzhong. I will march a hundred thousand foot and horse with the Uyghurs toward the Eastern Capital to coordinate our attack. If Your Majesty will cross the river with me and unite our strength to seize Daliang, I can then sweep west to take Gong and Shaan and join the Qin armies—the empire will be settled.

sentences.zh: 則王與趙王永無南慮，為唇齒之國，幸速計之。」

translations.literal: Then the King and the King of Zhao would forever be free of southern worries, lip-and-teeth allies—pray decide swiftly.
