translations.idiomatic: Then Your Majesty and the King of Zhao would never again fear attack from the south—you would be lip and teeth to each other. I beg you to decide quickly.

sentences.zh: 是時，悅聞天子已赦罪，復官爵，心不欲行，重遽絕滔，陽遣薛有倫報滔如約。

translations.literal: At this time Yue heard that the Son of Heaven had already pardoned his crimes and restored his titles; in his heart he did not wish to go. Yet he abruptly broke with Tao, while outwardly sending Xue Youlun to report to Tao as if keeping the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: By then Tian Yue had learned that the emperor had pardoned his crimes and restored his rank and titles. In his heart he had no wish to march. Yet he broke sharply with Zhu Tao while sending Xue Youlun to reply as though he still meant to keep their pact.

sentences.zh: 滔大喜，復使舍人李琯申固所言，悅猶豫，許士則諫曰：「冀王勇決權略，一世之雄也，殺懷仙，屠希彩，訹兄使如京師而奪之權，有恩者誅，同謀者覆，彼心腹渠可量哉？

translations.literal: Tao was greatly pleased and again sent his attendant Li Guan to reaffirm what had been said. Yue hesitated. Xu Shize remonstrated: The Prince of Ji is bold, decisive, and masterful in strategy—a hero of the age. He killed Huai Xian, slaughtered Xi Cai, coerced his elder brother to go to the capital and seized his power; those who owed him kindness he executed, co-conspirators he overthrew—how can that man's inmost heart be fathomed?
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao was delighted and sent his attendant Li Guan to confirm the plan once more. Tian Yue wavered. Xu Shize admonished him: The Prince of Ji is bold, decisive, and cunning—a hero of his generation. He killed Li Huaixian, butchered Li Xicai, and drove his own elder brother to the capital so he could seize power. He destroys those who show him kindness and turns on those who plotted with him. Who can read the depths of such a man?

sentences.zh: 今大王之親不加泚，勇不加懷仙、希彩也，而念恩不已，拘攣匹夫義，出且見禽。

translations.literal: Now the Great King's closeness to Ci does not surpass his ties to others, nor your valor to that of Huai Xian and Xi Cai—yet if you persist in gratitude without end, bound by a commoner's sense of obligation, once you go out you will be captured.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is no closer to Zhu Ci than others were, nor braver than Li Huaixian or Li Xicai. Yet if you cling to gratitude like some petty man of honor and go out to meet him, you will be taken.

sentences.zh: 彼得魏博，北聯幽薊，南入梁、鄭而與泚合，其理然也。

translations.literal: Once he obtains Weibo, linking north with You and Ji, entering south into Liang and Zheng and joining with Ci—that is only logical.
translations.idiomatic: Once he holds Weibo, joins the north with You and Ji, and drives south into Liang and Zheng to unite with Zhu Ci—that is exactly what reason dictates.

sentences.zh: 大王不如偽許出迎，遣州縣具牛酒，至則以事自解，不可顧恩取禍也。」

translations.literal: The Great King would do better to falsely promise to go out to meet him, order the prefectures and counties to prepare cattle and wine—and when he arrives, explain matters away on pretext; one must not court disaster for the sake of gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should feign agreement to go out and welcome him, order the prefectures and counties to prepare oxen and wine, and when he arrives plead necessity as your excuse. Do not invite ruin out of misplaced loyalty.

sentences.zh: 悅然之。

translations.literal: Yue agreed with this.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue accepted the advice.

sentences.zh: 先是，武俊陰約悅背滔，使相望。

translations.literal: Previously, Wujun had secretly agreed with Yue to turn against Tao, their forces keeping watch on one another.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wang Wujun had secretly agreed with Tian Yue to betray Zhu Tao, their armies keeping watch on each other.

sentences.zh: 及聞滔要悅西，使田秀馳說悅曰：「聞大王欲從滔度河，為泚掎角，非也。

translations.literal: When he heard that Tao wanted Yue to go west, he sent Tian Xiu in haste to persuade Yue, saying: I hear the Great King intends to follow Tao across the river and form pincers with Ci for him—that would be wrong.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Zhu Tao wanted Tian Yue to cross the river with him, he sent Tian Xiu in haste to dissuade him. I hear Your Majesty means to follow Zhu Tao across the river and serve as Zhu Ci's pincer—that would be a mistake, he said.

sentences.zh: 方泚未盜京師時，滔為列國，且自高，如得東都，與泚連禍，兵多勢張，返制於豎於乎？

translations.literal: While Ci had not yet seized the capital, Tao was one of the regional powers and already held himself high—if he takes the eastern capital, joined in shared fate with Ci, with vast troops and swelling might, would he then be controlled by that upstart?
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhu Ci even seized the capital, Zhu Tao already ranked among the great regional lords and thought himself above others. If he takes the Eastern Capital, binds his fate to Zhu Ci's, and commands a vast, swelling army—will he then submit to that upstart?

sentences.zh: 今日天子復官赦罪，乃王臣，豈舍天子而北面滔、泚耶！

translations.literal: Today the Son of Heaven has restored offices and pardoned crimes—they are the king's ministers. How could they abandon the Son of Heaven to turn north and submit to Tao and Ci!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor has restored their ranks and pardoned their crimes; they are the emperor's own ministers. Would they truly forsake the throne to bow north to Zhu Tao and Zhu Ci?

sentences.zh: 願大王閉壘不出，武俊須昭義軍出，為王討之。」

translations.literal: I pray Your Highness close the ramparts and do not come out. Wujun must wait for the Zhaoyi army to march forth and campaign on your behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness should hold the fort and stay within the walls. Wang Wujun must wait until the Zhaoyi army comes out to fight this war for you.

sentences.zh: 悅因秀還，具道其謀，而遣曾穆報滔。

translations.literal: Yue, taking advantage of Xiu's return, fully explained the plot, and dispatched Zeng Mu to report to Tao.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu returned, Tian Yue laid out the whole scheme in detail and sent Zeng Mu to inform Zhu Tao.

sentences.zh: 滔喜，自河間悉師而南，逾貝州，次清河，使人報悅，悅不至。

translations.literal: Tao rejoiced. From Hejian he led all his troops south, passed Beizhou, and halted at Qinghe. He sent men to notify Yue, but Yue did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao was delighted. From Hejian he marched his entire force south, crossed Beizhou, and encamped at Qinghe. He sent word to Tian Yue, but Yue never appeared.

sentences.zh: 進屯永濟，使王郅等督之曰：「王約出館陶與大王會，乃濟河。」

translations.literal: He advanced and encamped at Yongji, sending Wang Zhi and others to press him, saying: 'Our lord agreed to come out from Guantao to meet Your Highness, and then cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed on to Yongji and sent Wang Zhi and others to urge him on: 'Our lord promised to come out from Guantao and meet Your Highness before crossing the river together.

sentences.zh: 悅良久曰：「始約從王，今舉軍持悅曰：『魏比困侵掠，供擬屈竭。』

translations.literal: After a long silence Yue said: 'At first we agreed to follow our lord. Now the whole army holds Yue up and says: Wei has been worn down by raids and plunder; supplies and provisions are utterly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: After a long pause Tian Yue replied: 'We first agreed to march at our lord's side. Now the whole army confronts me and says: Wei has been ground down by constant raids and looting—our provisions are completely spent.

sentences.zh: 以悅日拊循，猶恐人且攜間，一日去城邑，朝出夕變，且何歸？

translations.literal: Though Yue daily comforts and reassures them, I still fear the people may yet turn disloyal. Leave the city for one day—march out in the morning and face mutiny by evening—and where would we return?
translations.idiomatic: Even though I comfort and reassure the men every day, I still fear they may turn against us. Leave the city for a single day—out in the morning, in revolt by evening—and where would we have left to go?

sentences.zh: 不然，悅不敢背約。

translations.literal: Otherwise, Yue would not dare break the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: If not for that, I would not dare break our pact.

sentences.zh: 今遣孟希祐悉兵五千助王。」

translations.literal: For now I am dispatching Meng Xiyou with five thousand troops in full to assist our lord.'
translations.idiomatic: For the moment I am sending Meng Xiyou with all five thousand of his troops to aid our lord.'

sentences.zh: 因使其屬裴抗、盧南史報命。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent his subordinates Pei Kang and Lu Nanshi to report this answer.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent his officers Pei Kang and Lu Nanshi back with this reply.

sentences.zh: 滔怒罵曰：「逆虜前日求救，許我貝州，我不取；

translations.literal: Tao raged and cursed: 'That rebel scum begged for rescue the other day and promised me Beizhou—I did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao flew into a rage and cursed: 'That rebel cur came begging for help the other day and promised me Beizhou—and I did not even take it.

sentences.zh: 尊我為天子，我與同為王；

translations.literal: They honored me as Son of Heaven; we were to be kings together.
translations.idiomatic: They proclaimed me Son of Heaven and pledged that we would reign as kings together.

sentences.zh: 教我遠來而不出。

translations.literal: They urged me to come from afar, yet now they will not come out.
translations.idiomatic: They summoned me from far away—and now they refuse to come out.

sentences.zh: 是賊不擊，尚何誅？」

translations.literal: If we do not strike such traitors, what is there left to punish?
translations.idiomatic: If traitors like these go unstruck, what villainy is left worth punishing?

sentences.zh: 乃囚抗等，使馬寔取數縣，已而釋抗還之，悅兵不敢出，遂圍貝州。

translations.literal: He then imprisoned Kang and the others, sent Ma Shi to seize several counties, and shortly after released Kang and sent them back. Yue's troops dared not sally forth, and Tao proceeded to besiege Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He imprisoned Kang and the rest, sent Ma Shi to overrun several counties, then soon released Kang and his party and sent them back. Tian Yue's troops dared not venture out, and Zhu Tao laid siege to Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 滔取武城，通德、棣，供軍饋，盡囚諸縣官吏，唯清陽不下，滔圍之。

translations.literal: Tao took Wucheng, Tongde, and Di, looted them for army provisions, and imprisoned all the county officials. Only Qingyang did not submit, and Tao besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao seized Wucheng, Tongde, and Di, stripping them for army supplies, and imprisoned every county official he could lay hands on. Only Qingyang held out, and he laid siege to it as well.

sentences.zh: 寔拔清平，殺五百人，俘男女貲財去。

translations.literal: Shi captured Qingping, killed five hundred people, and carried off men and women as captives along with goods and valuables.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shi stormed Qingping, slaughtered five hundred people, and marched off with captives—men and women alike—and all their goods and wealth.

sentences.zh: 於是李抱真、武俊約出兵救魏。

translations.literal: Thereupon Li Baozhen and Wujun agreed to lead troops to rescue Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baozhen and Wang Wujun then agreed to march out and relieve Wei.

sentences.zh: 會有詔拜悅檢校尚書右仆射，封濟陽郡王，而給事中孔巢父持節宣勞。

translations.literal: Just then an edict arrived appointing Yue as Acting Right Vice Minister of Works and enfeoffing him as Prince of Jiyang Commandery, while the Supervising Secretary Kong Chaofu came bearing credentials to proclaim the imperial favor and comfort the troops.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment an imperial edict arrived appointing Tian Yue Acting Right Vice Minister of Works and enfeoffing him as Prince of Jiyang, while the Supervising Secretary Kong Chaofu arrived with imperial credentials to announce the grace of the throne and comfort the army.

sentences.zh: 始悅阻兵凡四年，狂愎少謀，亟戰數北，死者什八，士苦之，且厭兵。

translations.literal: From the beginning Yue had held out with arms for four years in all. Arrogant and obstinate, lacking in strategy, he fought repeatedly and was defeated many times. The dead amounted to eight-tenths; the soldiers suffered bitterly and had grown weary of war.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue had kept his arms raised for four years altogether—arrogant, stubborn, and short on strategy. Battle after battle ended in defeat; eight men in ten were dead. The troops had suffered beyond endurance and were sick of war.

sentences.zh: 既巢父至，莫不欣然。

translations.literal: Once Chaofu arrived, none failed to rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: When Kong Chaofu arrived, every man rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 悅與巢父張飲，門階皆徹衛。

translations.literal: Yue drank expansively with Chaofu, and all guards were removed from the gates and steps.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue held a grand banquet with Kong Chaofu, and every guard was pulled from the gates and stairways.

sentences.zh: 至夜分，從弟緒與族人私語曰：「仆射妄起兵，幾赤吾族。

translations.literal: When night was deep, his younger cousin Xu privately spoke with clansmen, saying: 'The Vice Minister rashly raised troops and nearly exterminated our entire clan.
translations.idiomatic: Deep into the night, his younger cousin Tian Xu whispered with kinsmen: 'The Vice Minister raised arms without cause and nearly wiped our whole clan from the earth.

sentences.zh: 以金帛厚天下，而不至兄弟。」

translations.literal: He lavished gold and silk on the whole empire, yet gave nothing to his own brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He showered gold and silk on the whole world, yet never so much as reached his own brothers.

sentences.zh: 或諫止之，緒怒，殺諫者，乃與左右逾垣入。

translations.literal: Someone tried to dissuade him; Xu in anger killed the admonisher, then with his close companions scaled the wall and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Someone tried to stop him. Tian Xu in a fury killed the man who spoke up, then climbed the wall with his closest followers and went in.

sentences.zh: 悅方醉，寢酣。

translations.literal: Yue was drunk and sleeping soundly.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue was drunk and sleeping deeply.

sentences.zh: 緒挺刃升堂，二弟諫止，緒斬之，因手刺悅，並殺基母妻。

translations.literal: Xu drew his blade and ascended the hall. Two younger brothers tried to stop him; Xu cut them down, then personally stabbed Yue, and also killed his stepmother and wife.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xu drew his sword and mounted the hall. Two younger brothers tried to intervene; he cut them down, then drove the blade into Tian Yue himself, and killed his stepmother and wife as well.

sentences.zh: 悅死，年三十四。

translations.literal: Yue died at the age of thirty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue died at thirty-four.

sentences.zh: 比明，以悅命召許士則、蔡濟計事，至則殺之。

translations.literal: By dawn he summoned Xu Shize and Cai Ji in Yue's name to discuss affairs; when they arrived, he killed them.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak he summoned Xu Shize and Cai Ji in Tian Yue's name to consult on affairs of state—and killed them the moment they arrived.

sentences.zh: 劉忠信者，悅常使防督緒直寢門，緒呼曰：「忠信刺仆射，與扈反。」

translations.literal: Liu Zhongxin—Yue had often posted him on guard, supervising Xu at the bedchamber gate. Xu cried out: 'Zhongxin stabbed the Vice Minister and is conspiring rebellion with Hu!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhongxin—whom Tian Yue had regularly posted to guard the bedchamber door and keep watch over Tian Xu—Xu now shouted: 'Zhongxin stabbed the Vice Minister! He is in league with Hu to rebel!

sentences.zh: 眾執之，語曰：「無之。」

translations.literal: The crowd seized him. He spoke: 'It is not so.'
translations.idiomatic: The men seized him. He cried: 'It is not true!'

sentences.zh: 支已殊絕。

translations.literal: His limbs were already completely severed.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could finish, they had already hacked him limb from limb.

sentences.zh: 緒字緒，承嗣第六子。

translations.literal: Xu, courtesy name Xu, was the sixth son of Chengsi.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xu, styled Xu, was the sixth son of Tian Chengsi.

sentences.zh: 悅待諸弟無所間，使緒主牙軍，而兇險多過，嘗笞勖之。

translations.literal: Yue treated his younger brothers without suspicion, put Xu in charge of the headquarters guard, but Xu was vicious and reckless in many ways, and Yue had once flogged him as discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue treated his younger brothers without reserve and put Tian Xu in command of the headquarters guard, but Xu was cruel and reckless by nature, and Yue had once beaten him with the whip as punishment.

sentences.zh: 悅於飲食衣服，儉嗇有節，緒常苦不足，頗怨望，故作難。

translations.literal: Yue was frugal and restrained in food, drink, and clothing. Xu often felt the lack and harbored resentment, hence he staged this coup.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue was sparing and disciplined in food, drink, and dress. Tian Xu always felt himself shortchanged and nursed a deep grievance—and so he made his move.

sentences.zh: 悅既死，懼眾不附，以其徒數百將出奔，邢曹俊率眾追還。

translations.literal: After Yue died, Xu feared the masses would not follow him. With several hundred of his followers he was about to flee, but Xing Caojun led the troops in pursuit and brought him back.
translations.idiomatic: After Tian Yue's death, Tian Xu feared the army would not rally to him. He was about to flee with a few hundred of his own men when Xing Caojun led the troops after him and brought him back.

sentences.zh: 緒乃下令軍中曰：「我先王子，能立我者賞。」

translations.literal: Xu then issued an order throughout the army: 'I am the late Prince's son—whoever can establish me shall be rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xu then proclaimed to the army: 'I am the late prince's own son. Whoever helps establish my rule will be richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 眾乃共推緒為留後，歸罪扈，斬其首以徇。

translations.literal: The troops together proclaimed Xu as acting governor, shifted blame onto Hu, and beheaded him as a public warning.
translations.idiomatic: The men together acclaimed Tian Xu as acting governor, pinned the crime on Hu, and beheaded him as a public example.

sentences.zh: 復殺悅親信薛有倫等數十人，因巢父遣使者聽命天子。

translations.literal: He also killed several dozen of Yue's close confidants including Xue Youlun, and through Chaofu sent envoys to accept orders from the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to kill several dozen of Tian Yue's trusted men, including Xue Youlun, and through Kong Chaofu sent envoys to submit to the emperor's command.

sentences.zh: 滔聞悅死，以兵五千合寔軍，進攻魏州。

translations.literal: When Tao heard of Yue's death, he joined Shi's army with five thousand troops and advanced to attack Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Tao learned of Tian Yue's death, he combined five thousand of his own troops with Ma Shi's force and marched on Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 寔瀕王莽河壁，南距河，東抵博州，殺略甚眾。

translations.literal: Shi entrenched along the Wang Mang River, with the river to the south and Buzhou to the east, killing and plundering on a vast scale.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shi fortified his line along the Wang Mang River—the river at his back to the south, Buzhou to the east—and killed and looted without mercy.

sentences.zh: 使人入魏招緒降。

translations.literal: He sent men into Wei to summon Xu to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys into Wei to demand Tian Xu's surrender.

sentences.zh: 緒新篡，而寔圍且急，乃遣使以好言見滔，滔許與盟。

translations.literal: Xu, having just seized power, found Shi's siege pressing close, and so sent envoys with friendly words to see Tao; Tao agreed to ally with him.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xu had only just seized power, and with Ma Shi's siege tightening by the day, he sent envoys with conciliatory words to Zhu Tao—who agreed to treat with him.

sentences.zh: 曾穆勸緒絕滔，而緒部分亦定，乃乘城戰，武俊、抱真各脩好如悅時。

translations.literal: Zeng Mu urged Xu to break with Tao, but once Xu's forces were also stabilized, he took to the walls and fought. Wujun and Baozhen each restored friendly relations as in Yue's time.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Mu urged Tian Xu to break with Zhu Tao, but once his own ranks were steady he fought from the walls. Wang Wujun and Li Baozhen each renewed their alliance with Wei, just as in Tian Yue's day.

sentences.zh: 詔即拜緒節度使。

translations.literal: An edict immediately appointed Xu as military governor.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict promptly confirmed Tian Xu as military governor.

sentences.zh: 寔圍魏凡三月，滔敗走。

translations.literal: Shi besieged Wei for three months in all; Tao was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shi besieged Wei for three months altogether before Zhu Tao was beaten and driven off.

sentences.zh: 累遷檢校尚書左仆射、常山郡王，又徙王雁門，實封五百戶，加同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Acting Left Vice Minister of Works and Prince of Changshan Commandery, then transferred to Prince of Yanmen, with an actual fief of five hundred households, and additionally made Grand Councilor of the State Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to Acting Left Vice Minister of Works and Prince of Changshan, then transferred to Prince of Yanmen with a substantive fief of five hundred households, and further granted the title of Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 暴疾死，年三十三，贈司空。

translations.literal: He died suddenly of illness at thirty-three, and was posthumously granted the title of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died suddenly of illness at thirty-three; the court posthumously enfeoffed him as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 少子季安嗣。

translations.literal: His youngest son Ji'an succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son, Tian Ji'an, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 會詔中尉吐突承璀以神策兵討王承宗，季安謀曰：「王師不跨河二十五年，今越魏伐趙，趙誠虜，魏亦虜矣，奈何？」

translations.literal: Just then an edict ordered the Chief Eunuch Tuhu Chenghuang to lead the Shence Army against Wang Chengzong. Ji'an counseled: 'Imperial troops have not crossed the river in twenty-five years. Now to cross Wei to attack Zhao—even if Zhao is indeed subdued, Wei too will be lost. What is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: Just then an edict dispatched the Chief Eunuch Tuhu Chenghuang with the Shence Army to campaign against Wang Chengzong. Tian Ji'an counseled: 'Imperial armies have not crossed the river in twenty-five years. To march through Wei to strike Zhao—even if Zhao is truly brought to heel, Wei will be lost as well. What are we to do?

sentences.zh: 或請以五千騎決除君憂。

translations.literal: Some also proposed resolving Your Lordship's worry with five thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Some even urged that five thousand cavalry might settle the matter at a stroke and lift his cares.

sentences.zh: 季安曰：「善，沮軍者斬！」

translations.literal: Ji'an said: 'Good—whoever discourages the army, behead him!
translations.idiomatic: Ji'an replied, 'Agreed. Anyone who hampers the campaign dies!

sentences.zh: 時幽州劉濟將譚忠適使魏，聞之，入見季安曰：「往年王師取蜀取吳，算不失一，是宰相謀也。

translations.literal: At that time Tan Zhong, a commander under Liu Ji of Youzhou, happened to be on mission to Wei; hearing this, he went in to see Ji'an and said: 'In former years when the royal armies took Shu and Wu, not one plan failed—that was the chancellor's stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Tan Zhong, a commander serving Liu Ji of Youzhou, happened to be in Wei on an embassy. When he heard of this, he went to see Ji'an and said, 'When the imperial armies conquered Shu and Wu in years past, not a single stratagem failed—that was the work of chancellors at court.

sentences.zh: 今伐趙，不使耆臣宿將而付中臣，不起天下甲而出秦甲，君知誰為之謀？

translations.literal: Now in attacking Zhao, not using elder ministers and veteran generals but entrusting it to middling officials, not raising armor from under Heaven but sending out Qin armor—does my lord know whose plan this is?
translations.idiomatic: This campaign against Zhao—veteran statesmen and seasoned generals are passed over in favor of lesser courtiers; troops are not mobilized from across the realm but drawn from Guanzhong alone. Do you know whose design this is?

sentences.zh: 此上自為謀，以誇服臣下。

translations.literal: This is the sovereign planning for himself, to boast and make his ministers submit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is scheming for himself—to dazzle and cow his own officials.

sentences.zh: 若師未叩趙，而先碎於魏，是上之謀不及下，且能不恥！

translations.literal: If the army has not yet assaulted Zhao but is first broken at Wei, then the sovereign's stratagem cannot match those below—and can he not feel shame!
translations.idiomatic: If the army reaches Zhao's borders only after being shattered at Wei, the emperor's strategy will have proved inferior to those beneath him—and will he not be mortified?

sentences.zh: 既恥且怒，必任智畫，仗猛將，再舉涉河。

translations.literal: Having both shame and anger, he will certainly employ wise plans and rely on fierce generals, again raising troops to cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: Once shamed and enraged, he will surely enlist sharper counsel, commit his fiercest generals, and launch another crossing of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 鑒前之敗，必不越魏誅趙；

translations.literal: Reflecting on the previous defeat, he will certainly not pass over Wei to punish Zhao;
translations.idiomatic: Chastened by the last defeat, he will not bypass Wei to strike at Zhao;

sentences.zh: 校罪輕重，必不先趙後魏。

translations.literal: Comparing the weight of guilt, he will certainly not put Zhao before Wei.
translations.idiomatic: weighing which side bears the heavier guilt, he will certainly not move against Zhao before Wei.

sentences.zh: 是上不上，下不下，當魏而來也。」

translations.literal: Thus neither ascending nor descending, he will come directly against Wei.'
translations.idiomatic: Caught between advancing and retreating, he will march straight on Wei.'

sentences.zh: 季安曰：「計安出？」

translations.literal: Ji'an said: 'From where does the plan emerge?'
translations.idiomatic: Ji'an asked, 'What is your counsel?'

sentences.zh: 忠曰：「王師入魏，君厚犒之。

translations.literal: Zhong said: 'When the royal army enters Wei, my lord should richly reward them.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Zhong replied, 'When the imperial troops enter Wei, treat them with lavish hospitality.

sentences.zh: 悉甲伐趙，而陰遺趙書曰：『魏若伐趙，為賣友；

translations.literal: With all armor attack Zhao, but secretly send Zhao a letter saying: "If Wei attacks Zhao, it is selling out a friend;
translations.idiomatic: Then march in full force against Zhao—but secretly send Zhao a letter saying, "If Wei joins in attacking Zhao, it betrays a friend;

sentences.zh: 魏若與趙，為反君。

translations.literal: If Wei joins with Zhao, it is turning against the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: if Wei stands with Zhao, it rebels against the throne.

sentences.zh: 賣友反君，魏不忍受。

translations.literal: Selling out a friend and turning against the sovereign—Wei cannot endure it.
translations.idiomatic: Betrayal on one hand, treason on the other—Wei cannot endure either charge.

sentences.zh: 執事能弛陴鄣，遺一城，魏得持之獻捷天子以為符，此使魏北得以奉趙，西得以為臣，不世之利也。』

translations.literal: If the minister can relax ramparts and bastions and cede one city, Wei can hold it to present triumph to the Son of Heaven as token—this enables Wei to serve Zhao in the north and be a subject in the west—profit not of this age.
translations.idiomatic: If you would lift your defenses and yield one city, Wei can take it and present it to the Son of Heaven as proof of victory—letting Wei honor Zhao in the north while playing the loyal subject in the west. A prize beyond price.

sentences.zh: 趙不拒君，則魏安矣。」

translations.literal: If Zhao does not reject my lord, then Wei is secure.
translations.idiomatic: If Zhao does not rebuff you, Wei is saved.

sentences.zh: 季安然之，遣大將率兵會王師伐承宗，糧餉自辦，取堂陽以報，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Ji'an approved, dispatched a great general leading troops to join the royal army in attacking Cheng Zong, provisions self-supplied, took Tangyang to report, and was added as Grand Guardian of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Ji'an agreed. He dispatched a senior general at the head of his troops to join the imperial campaign against Wang Chengzong, supplied his own provisions, seized Tangyang in repayment, and was appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 有丘絳者，父時賓佐，與同府侯臧爭權，季安怒，斥為下縣尉，俄召還，先坎道左，既至，生瘞之。

translations.literal: There was one Qiu Jiang, a guest-assistant from his father's time, who contended for power with Hou Zang of the same command; Ji'an in anger demoted him to a lower county captain, soon summoned him back, first dug a pit on the left of the road, and when he arrived, buried him alive.
translations.idiomatic: One Qiu Jiang, a retainer from his father's day, had jockeyed for power with a fellow officer named Hou Zang. Ji'an flew into a rage, banished Qiu to a lowly county post as assistant magistrate—then summoned him back, had a pit dug by the roadside, and when Qiu arrived, buried him alive.

sentences.zh: 忍酷無忌憚，大抵如此，死年三十二，贈太尉。

translations.literal: Cruel without restraint or fear—mostly thus; died at thirty-two, posthumously granted Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his savage, unbridled cruelty. He died at thirty-two and was posthumously ennobled as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 妻元誼女，召諸將立其子懷諫，最幼，不能事，政決於私奴蔣士則，數易置諸將，軍中怒，取田興為留後，所謂田弘正者，以懷諫歸第，殺士則等十餘人。

translations.literal: His wife was Yuan Yi's daughter; he summoned the generals to establish his son Huaijian, the youngest, unable to manage affairs; government was decided by the private slave Jiang Shize; repeatedly changed and replaced generals; the army grew angry, made Tian Xing acting commander—the one called Tian Hongzheng—sent Huaijian back to his residence, and killed Shize and more than ten others.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was a daughter of Yuan Yi. The generals were summoned to install his youngest son, Huaijian—still a child, unable to rule. Real power fell to a household slave, Jiang Shize, who shuffled commanders at whim until the troops revolted. They installed Tian Xing—later known as Tian Hongzheng—as acting military governor, sent Huaijian home, and put Jiang Shize and a dozen others to death.

sentences.zh: 季安既葬，送懷諫京師，授右監門衛將軍，寵錫蕃渥。

translations.literal: After Ji'an was buried, Huaijian was sent to the capital, appointed Right Gate Guard General, favors and gifts luxuriant and thick.
translations.idiomatic: After Ji'an's burial, Huaijian was escorted to the capital and made a general of the Right Gate Guard, showered with imperial favors.

sentences.zh: 緒弟縉、華顯於朝。

translations.literal: Ji's younger brothers Jin and Hua were conspicuous at court.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's younger brothers Jin and Hua both rose to prominence at court.

sentences.zh: 縉字雲長，貞元十年入朝，授左驍衛將軍，封扶風郡公。

translations.literal: Jin, courtesy name Yunzhang, in the tenth year of Zhenyuan entered court, was appointed Left Valiant Cavalry General, and was enfeoffed Duke of Fufeng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, styled Yunzhang, came to court in the tenth year of the Zhenyuan reign and was appointed Left Valiant Cavalry General and created Duke of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 元和中，拜夏綏銀節度使。

translations.literal: During Yuanhe, he was appointed military commissioner of the Xia-Sui-Yin circuit.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe era, he was made military commissioner of the Xia-Sui-Yin circuit.

sentences.zh: 始開元時，置宥州，扼寇路，久而廢，縉復城之。

translations.literal: Originally in the Kaiyuan era You Prefecture was established to block invader routes; long since abandoned, Jin rebuilt its walls.
translations.idiomatic: You Prefecture had been established in the Kaiyuan era to block barbarian incursions, but had long lain in ruins; Jin restored its fortifications.

sentences.zh: 王師伐蔡，縉上橐它牛馬助軍。

translations.literal: When the royal army attacked Cai, Jin presented pack camels, oxen, and horses to assist the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army marched on Cai, Jin sent pack camels, oxen, and horses to support the campaign.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃寇豐州，縉設伏邀其歸，俘斬過當。

translations.literal: Tibetans raided Feng Prefecture; Jin set an ambush to intercept their return; captives and beheadings exceeded the count.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans raided Feng Prefecture, Jin laid an ambush along their retreat and killed or captured far more than he lost.

sentences.zh: 入為左衛大將軍，李聽代之。

translations.literal: He entered court as Left Guard Grand General; Li Ting replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Grand General of the Left Guard; Li Ting succeeded him in the field.

sentences.zh: 聽劾縉盜沒軍糧四萬斛，強取羌人羊馬，故吐蕃得乘隙。

translations.literal: Ting impeached Jin for stealing and embezzling forty thousand hu of army grain and forcibly seizing Qiang people's sheep and horses, thus Tibetans could seize the opening.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ting accused Jin of diverting forty thousand bushels of military grain and seizing sheep and horses from the Qiang—leaving the frontier porous enough for Tibetan raiders to strike through.

sentences.zh: 貶衡王傅。

translations.literal: He was demoted to Tutor of the Prince of Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was demoted to tutor to the Prince of Heng.

sentences.zh: 俄而吐蕃又攻鹽州，貶房州司馬。

translations.literal: Soon after, Tibetans again attacked Yan Prefecture, and he was demoted to Vice Administrator of Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans attacked Yan Prefecture again soon after, he was further demoted to vice administrator of Fang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，終左領軍衛將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing, he died while holding the post of Left Army Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Changqing era, he died while serving as Left Army Guard General.

sentences.zh: 華，太常少卿，尚永樂、新都二公主。

translations.literal: Hua was Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and married the two princesses of Yongle and Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: Hua served as Vice Minister of Rites and married two imperial princesses—those of Yongle and Xindu.

sentences.zh: 田氏自承嗣至懷諫，四世，凡四十九年。

translations.literal: The Tian clan from Chengsi to Huaijian: four generations, altogether forty-nine years.
translations.idiomatic: From Chengsi to Huaijian, the Tian family held power for four generations over forty-nine years.

sentences.zh: 史憲誠，其先奚也，內徙靈武，為建康人。

translations.literal: Shi Xiancheng—his forebears were Xi; internally resettled at Lingwu, they became people of Jian' Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiancheng's ancestors were Khitan Xi who had been resettled inland at Lingwu; his family were natives of Jian' Kang.

sentences.zh: 三世署魏博將，祖及父爵皆為王。

translations.literal: For three generations they were appointed Wei-Bo generals; grandfather and father were both ennobled as kings.
translations.idiomatic: For three generations his family held generalships in Weibo; both his grandfather and father were ennobled as kings.

sentences.zh: 憲誠始以趫敢從父軍，田弘正討李師道，將先鋒兵四千濟河，拔城柵，師踵進，乘勝逐北，傅鄆堞。

translations.literal: Xiancheng first, for swift daring, followed his father's army; when Tian Hongzheng campaigned against Li Shidao, he led four thousand vanguard troops across the river, stormed walled stockades, the army followed in succession, rode victory in pursuit northward, and pressed against the battlements of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng first won notice for his daring in his father's campaigns. When Tian Hongzheng marched against Li Shidao, he led four thousand vanguard troops across the river, stormed fortified stockades, and pressed the pursuit northward until his lines hugged the walls of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 師道傳首，以功兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: Li Shidao's head was transmitted; for merit he was concurrently appointed Vice Censor in Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shidao's head was sent to court, Xiancheng was rewarded with the concurrent post of Vice Censor in Chief.

sentences.zh: 長慶二年，田布之自殺也，軍亂且囂。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changqing, when Tian Bu killed himself, the army was mutinous and clamorous.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changqing, after Tian Bu took his own life, the army fell into uproar and rebellion.

sentences.zh: 時憲誠為中軍兵馬使，頗言河朔舊事以搖其眾，眾乃逼還府，擅總軍務。

translations.literal: At that time Xiancheng was Middle Army Horse-and-Infantry Commissioner; he frequently spoke of old Heshuo affairs to sway the troops; the masses then forced their way back to headquarters and usurped overall military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng, then commander of the middle army, stirred the troops with tales of old Hebei grievances until they forced their way back to headquarters and seized control of the command.

sentences.zh: 穆宗以朱克融、王廷湊方盜幽、鎮，未有以制，即以節度使授之。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong, as Zhu Kerong and Wang Tingcou were just plundering You and Zhen and he had no means to control them, therefore granted him the military commissionership.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhu Kerong and Wang Tingcou already raiding You and Zhen, Emperor Muzong had no leverage left—and confirmed Xiancheng as military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 憲誠外詫王命，而陰結幽、鎮，依以自固。

translations.literal: Xiancheng outwardly feigned royal command, but secretly allied with You and Zhen and relied on them to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng paid lip service to the throne while secretly aligning with You and Zhen, using them to buttress his own position.

sentences.zh: 時李方亂，私與交通，數助請旄節，城馬頭，具舟黎陽，示將濟師者。

translations.literal: At that time the Li faction was in disorder; he privately communicated with them, repeatedly helped request banners and batons, walled Matou, prepared boats at Liyang, and showed intent to cross troops.
translations.idiomatic: While the court faction loyal to Li was in disarray, he maintained secret ties with them, repeatedly lobbying for a formal commission, fortified Matou, and readied boats at Liyang as though preparing a river crossing.

sentences.zh: 會天子遣司門郎中韋文恪宣慰，憲誠見使者禮倨，言辭悖慢。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven dispatched Gate Section Director Wei Wenke to proclaim consolation, Xiancheng upon meeting the envoy was ritually arrogant and his words defiant and insolent.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor dispatched Wei Wenke of the Ministry of Rites to announce imperial condolences, Xiancheng received the envoy with brazen disrespect and answered with open insolence.

sentences.zh: 俄聞斬，更恭謹謂文恪曰：「我本奚，如狗也，唯知識主，雖日加箠不忍離。」

translations.literal: Soon hearing of execution, he became more respectful and deferential and told Wenke: 'I am originally Xi, like a dog—only know to recognize a master; though flogged daily, I cannot bear to leave.
translations.idiomatic: When word spread that heads would roll, he turned meek and told Wei Wenke, 'I am a Xi by birth—no better than a dog that knows only its master. Beat me every day and still I would not leave his side.

sentences.zh: 其譎獪類此。

translations.literal: His deceit and craftiness were like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the tenor of his cunning.

sentences.zh: 進檢校司空。

translations.literal: He was promoted to honorary Grand Master of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to honorary Grand Master of Works.

sentences.zh: 與李全略為婚家，大和中，其子同捷反，潛以糧餉資之。

translations.literal: He was connected by marriage to Li Quanlue; in Dahe his son Tongjie rebelled, and he secretly supplied provisions to support him.
translations.idiomatic: He was connected by marriage to Li Quanlue; during the Dahe era, when Li's son Tongjie rose in rebellion, Xiancheng secretly fed his army.

sentences.zh: 文宗申約，使者相望，因進同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong reiterated the covenant; envoys came one after another in sight of each other; therefore he was promoted concurrently Associate Counselor of the Central Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong reaffirmed their pact—envoys shuttled back and forth in an unbroken stream—and Xiancheng was elevated to Associate Counselor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 憲誠使大將至京師偵事，作謾言自大，宰相韋處厚折其詐，遣去。

translations.literal: Xiancheng sent a great general to the capital to spy on affairs, making boastful arrogant speech; Chancellor Wei Chuhou exposed his fraud and had him sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng dispatched a senior general to the capital to gather intelligence. The man swaggered and spoke with flagrant arrogance until Chancellor Wei Chuhou saw through the deception and sent him packing.

sentences.zh: 憲誠懼，出兵從王師討之，復遣大將丌志沼率師二萬攻德州。

translations.literal: Xiancheng feared, deployed troops to follow the imperial army in suppressing them, and again sent the great general Qizhao at the head of twenty thousand troops to attack De Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Xiancheng marched out with the imperial forces to suppress the rebellion and again dispatched his general Qizhao with twenty thousand men to attack De Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時王廷湊援同捷，陰誘志沼以利。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Tingcou was aiding Tongjie and secretly enticed Qizhao with profit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingcou, then aiding Tongjie, secretly tempted Qizhao with promises of profit.

sentences.zh: 志沼反，屯永濟，兵銳甚，諸鎮共禦之。

translations.literal: Qizhao rebelled, encamped at Yongji, his troops very sharp; the various commands jointly resisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Qizhao turned traitor, encamped at Yongji with a fierce and crack army, and the surrounding commands united to hold him at bay.

sentences.zh: 憲誠告急，天子詔義武李聽進討。

translations.literal: Xiancheng reported emergency; the Son of Heaven ordered Li Ting of Yiwu to advance in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng sent urgent appeals for help, and the emperor ordered Li Ting of Yiwu to march against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 於是志沼與廷湊合兵劫貝州，為聽所敗，奔廷湊。

translations.literal: Thereupon Qizhao joined forces with Tingcou to raid Bei Prefecture, was defeated by Li Ting, and fled to Tingcou.
translations.idiomatic: Qizhao then united with Tingcou to plunder Bei Prefecture, but Li Ting routed them, and Qizhao fled to Tingcou's camp.

sentences.zh: 滄景平，憲誠不自安，請納地，進檢校司徒兼侍中，徙河中，封千乘郡公，以李聽代。

translations.literal: When Cang and Jing were pacified, Xiancheng felt insecure, requested to surrender territory, was promoted to Honorary Minister of Education and concurrently Palace Attendant, transferred to Hezhong, enfeoffed Duke of Qiansheng Commandery, with Li Ting replacing him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Cang and Jing were pacified, Xiancheng no longer felt secure in his seat. He offered to surrender his territory and was promoted to Honorary Minister of Education with the concurrent rank of Palace Attendant, transferred to Hezhong, and created Duke of Qiansheng, while Li Ting took his place at Weibo.

sentences.zh: 初，憲誠將以族行，懼魏軍之留，問策於弟憲忠，憲忠教分相、衛，請置帥，因以弱魏。

translations.literal: Initially, Xiancheng intended to relocate with his clan, fearing the Wei army would detain them; he asked counsel from his younger brother Xianzhong, who advised dividing Xiang and Wei, requesting the appointment of commanders, thereby to weaken Wei.
translations.idiomatic: At first Xiancheng planned to move his entire clan, fearing the men of Wei would hold them back. He consulted his brother Xianzhong, who advised petitioning the throne to split off Xiang and Wei into separate commands with their own governors—thus sapping Weibo's strength.

sentences.zh: 復請詔聽引軍聲圖志沼而假道清河，帝從之。

translations.literal: He again requested an edict that Li Ting lead troops, ostensibly to target Qizhao but borrowing passage through Qinghe; the Emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: He further petitioned that Li Ting be ordered to march—ostensibly against Qizhao, but in reality to pass through Qinghe on the way. The emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 憲誠因欲倚聽公去魏，及聽次清河，魏人驚，憲忠曰：「彼假道取賊，吾軍無負朝廷，何懼為？」

translations.literal: Xiancheng thus wished to rely on Lord Ting to leave Wei; when Li Ting halted at Qinghe, the people of Wei were alarmed. Xianzhong said: 'They borrow passage to capture rebels; our army has not betrayed the court—what is there to fear?'
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng meant to use Li Ting's departure to clear him from Wei. When Li Ting encamped at Qinghe, the people of Wei panicked. Xianzhong said, 'He is only borrowing the road to strike at rebels. Our army has done the court no wrong—what do we have to fear?

sentences.zh: 乃稍安。

translations.literal: Thus they gradually calmed.
translations.idiomatic: With that, tempers eased a little.

sentences.zh: 然魏素聚兵清河，聽至，悉出其甲，將入魏，魏軍聞之懼，明日盡甲而出。

translations.literal: Yet Wei had long massed troops at Qinghe; when Li Ting arrived, they all donned armor, about to enter Wei; hearing this the Wei army feared, and the next day they all armored and came out.
translations.idiomatic: But Weibo had long kept a concentration of troops at Qinghe. When Li Ting arrived, they all took up their armor as though he meant to invade Wei itself. The garrison was terrified, and the next morning every man marched out in full battle gear.

sentences.zh: 聽按軍館陶不進。

translations.literal: Li Ting halted his army at Guantao and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ting held his army at Guantao and made no move forward.

sentences.zh: 眾謂憲誠賣己，曰：「紿我以沽恩耶？」

translations.literal: The masses said Xiancheng had sold them out, saying: 'You deceived us to buy favor, did you?'
translations.idiomatic: The troops decided Xiancheng had betrayed them. 'Did you trick us just to curry favor with the court?' they cried.

sentences.zh: 夜攻殺之，並監軍史良佐，推何進滔為帥以請，詔贈憲誠太尉，實大和三年。

translations.literal: That night they attacked and killed him, also the supervising commissioner Shi Liangzuo, pushed He Jintao to be commander and petitioned; an edict posthumously granted Xiancheng Grand Preceptor, in the third year of Dahe.
translations.idiomatic: That night they stormed in and killed him, along with the supervising commissioner Shi Liangzuo. They proclaimed He Jintao their leader and petitioned the throne. An edict posthumously ennobled Xiancheng as Grand Preceptor. This was the third year of the Dahe reign.

sentences.zh: 憲誠起，凡七年，死。

translations.literal: From Xiancheng's rise, in all seven years, then death.
translations.idiomatic: From his rise to power until his death, Xiancheng ruled seven years.

sentences.zh: 何進滔，靈武人，世為本軍校。

translations.literal: He Jintao, a native of Lingwu, for generations served as officers of the local army.
translations.idiomatic: He Jintao was a native of Lingwu; for generations his family had served as officers in the garrison.

sentences.zh: 少客魏，委質軍中，事田弘正。

translations.literal: Young he sojourned in Wei, pledged himself in the army, and served Tian Hongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he lived as a guest in Wei, pledged himself to the army, and entered the service of Tian Hongzheng.

sentences.zh: 弘正攻王承宗，夜以兵壓鎮州。

translations.literal: Hongzheng attacked Wang Chengzong, at night pressing troops against Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongzheng campaigned against Wang Chengzong, he pressed Zhen Prefecture by night.

sentences.zh: 承宗使健將以鐵冒面，引精騎千餘馳魏壁。

translations.literal: Chengzong sent a stalwart general with iron covering his face, leading over a thousand elite cavalry to gallop against the Wei ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong sent a champion general whose face was masked in iron, at the head of a thousand picked horsemen, to charge the Wei lines.

sentences.zh: 進滔率猛士逐之，幾獲，鎮人大懼。

translations.literal: Jintao led fierce warriors in pursuit, nearly capturing him; the people of Zhen were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Jintao led his fiercest warriors in pursuit and nearly took him. The garrison at Zhen was seized with dread.

sentences.zh: 從討李師道，以功兼侍御史。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Li Shidao, for merit he was concurrently appointed Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Li Shidao he distinguished himself and was made concurrent Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 憲誠死，軍中傳謼曰：「得何公事之，軍安矣！」

translations.literal: When Xiancheng died, a rumor spread through the army saying: 'If we get Lord He to serve us, the army will be secure!'
translations.idiomatic: When Xiancheng died, a cry went up through the ranks: 'Get Lord He to lead us and this army will be at peace!

sentences.zh: 進滔下令曰：「公等既迫我，當聽吾令。」

translations.literal: Jintao issued an order saying: 'Since you gentlemen have forced me, you must obey my commands.'
translations.idiomatic: Jintao proclaimed, 'You have forced this on me—then you will obey my orders.'

sentences.zh: 眾唯唯。

translations.literal: The crowd assented one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The men murmured their assent.

sentences.zh: 「孰殺前使及監軍者，疏出之。」

translations.literal: 'Whoever killed the former commissioner and the supervising commissioner, list them out.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Name every man who took part in killing the former governor and the supervising commissioner.

sentences.zh: 凡斬九十餘人，釋脅從者。

translations.literal: In all over ninety were beheaded; those coerced into participation were released.
translations.idiomatic: More than ninety were executed. Those who had been compelled to follow were set free.

sentences.zh: 素服臨哭，將吏皆入吊。

translations.literal: Wearing plain mourning garb he presided over weeping; officers and clerks all came to pay condolences.
translations.idiomatic: He appeared in undyed mourning dress to weep over the dead, and every officer and official came to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 詔拜留後，俄進授節度使。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him acting governor; soon he was advanced to military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict confirmed him as acting governor; before long he received the full commission of military governor.

sentences.zh: 居魏十餘年，民安之。

translations.literal: He dwelt in Wei for more than ten years; the people found peace under him.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Wei for more than a decade, and the people lived in quiet under his rule.

sentences.zh: 進累檢校司徒、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Honorary Minister of Education and Associate Counselor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive honors to Honorary Minister of Education and Associate Counselor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 開成五年死，贈太傅，謚曰定。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaicheng he died; posthumously granted Grand Tutor, posthumous title Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Kaicheng, was posthumously ennobled Grand Tutor, and given the posthumous name Ding.

sentences.zh: 子全臯襲，明年，拜節度使。

translations.literal: His son Quangao succeeded; the next year he was appointed military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Quangao succeeded him and received the military commission the following year.

sentences.zh: 平龐勛，以功遷檢校司空、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Pacifying Pang Xun, for merit he was transferred to Honorary Grand Master of Works and Associate Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: After suppressing Pang Xun's rebellion he was promoted to Honorary Grand Master of Works and Associate Counselor.

sentences.zh: 母喪，納所賜節，願行喪，詔不許。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he returned the granted baton of office, wishing to observe mourning; an edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he surrendered his commissioner's baton, begging leave to mourn—but the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 全臯年少好殺戮，下有小罪，鮮縱貰，人人危懼。

translations.literal: Quangao was young and fond of killing; for minor offenses below him, he rarely showed pardon; everyone lived in dread.
translations.idiomatic: Quangao was young and bloodthirsty. Even petty infractions rarely escaped punishment, and every man under him lived in fear.

sentences.zh: 後軍中相傳晙減糧帛，眾遂叛，全臯單騎遁，眾推韓君雄以總軍事，而殺全臯，實咸通十一年。

translations.literal: Later a rumor spread through the army that supplies and pay were being cut; the crowd then rebelled; Quangao fled alone on horseback; the masses pushed Han Junxiong to oversee military affairs, and killed Quangao, in the eleventh year of Xiantong.
translations.idiomatic: Later a rumor spread through the army that supplies and pay were being cut. The men mutinied. Quangao fled alone on horseback. They installed Han Junxiong to command affairs and killed Quangao. This was the eleventh year of Xiantong.

sentences.zh: 詔贈太保。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously ennobled him Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 自進滔至全臯，凡三世，四十二年。

translations.literal: From Jintao to Quangao, three generations, forty-two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Jintao to Quangao, the He family held power for three generations over forty-two years.

sentences.zh: 懿宗更以普王為大使，擢君雄留後。

translations.literal: Emperor Yizong replaced with Prince Pu as grand envoy, promoted Junxiong as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yizong appointed Prince Pu as grand envoy and promoted Han Junxiong to acting governor.

sentences.zh: 君雄，魏州人。

translations.literal: Junxiong was a native of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Junxiong was a native of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 不五月，進副大使，三遷檢校司空。

translations.literal: Within five months, advanced to vice grand envoy, thrice promoted to Honorary Grand Master of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Within five months he was advanced to vice grand envoy and thrice promoted to Honorary Grand Master of Works.

sentences.zh: 僖宗即位，進同中書門下平章事，賜名允中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong ascended, promoted to Associate Counselor, granted name Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong took the throne, he was promoted to Associate Counselor and granted the name Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 死年六十一，贈太尉。

translations.literal: Died at sixty-one, posthumously Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-one and was posthumously ennobled Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 子簡，襲留後。

translations.literal: Son Jian succeeded as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jian succeeded him as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 俄授節度使，進累檢校太尉、同中書門下平章事，封魏郡王。

translations.literal: Soon appointed military commissioner, promoted to Honorary Grand Preceptor and Associate Counselor, enfeoffed Prince of Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon confirmed as military commissioner, promoted to Honorary Grand Preceptor and Associate Counselor, and created Prince of Wei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 帝在蜀，天下亂，簡恃強完，欲拓地，覬望非常。

translations.literal: The emperor was in Shu, the realm in chaos; Jian relied on his strength and completeness, wished to expand territory, harbored extraordinary ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: With the emperor in exile in Shu and the realm in chaos, Jian trusted in his own strength and security, sought to expand his territory, and nursed ambitions beyond his station.

sentences.zh: 時諸葛爽為黃巢守河陽，簡攻之，爽走，即戍以兵，以略邢、洺而歸。

translations.literal: At that time Zhuge Shuang held Heyang for Huang Chao; Jian attacked, Shuang fled, he garrisoned with troops, raided Xing and Mo and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhuge Shuang held Heyang for Huang Chao. Jian attacked, Shuang fled, and Jian left a garrison before raiding Xing and Mo and returning home.

sentences.zh: 東攻鄆，鄆將曹存實出戰，敗死，其將朱宣率眾以守，久不下，爽乘其隙，復取河陽。

translations.literal: He marched east against Yan; the Yan general Cao Cunshi rode out to fight and was killed in defeat; his subordinate Zhu Xuan led the masses to hold defense, long unable to take; Shuang seized the opening and again took Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: He marched east against Yan. The Yan general Cao Cunshi rode out to fight and was killed in defeat. His subordinate Zhu Xuan held the city, but the siege dragged on. Shuang seized the opening and retook Heyang.

sentences.zh: 簡還攻之，爽迎擊新鄉，簡大敗，樂彥禛以一軍先還，簡奔歸，疽發背死。

translations.literal: Jian returned to attack; Shuang intercepted him at Xingxiang; Jian suffered great defeat; Yue Yanzhen brought one division home first; Jian fled back and died of a back abscess.
translations.idiomatic: Jian returned to attack. Shuang intercepted him at Xingxiang. Jian suffered a crushing defeat. Yue Yanzhen brought one division home first. Jian fled back and died of a back abscess.

sentences.zh: 彥禎代之。

translations.literal: Yue Yanzhen replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yanzhen replaced him.

sentences.zh: 再世，凡十二年。

translations.literal: Two generations, twelve years in all.
translations.idiomatic: Two generations held power for twelve years in all.

sentences.zh: 彥禎者，亦魏人。

translations.literal: Yue Yanzhen was also a native of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yanzhen was also a native of Wei.

sentences.zh: 簡時，歷博州刺史，下河陽有功，遷澶州。

translations.literal: During Jian's time he had served as prefect of Bo, distinguished himself descending on Heyang, transferred to Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Jian's time he had served as prefect of Bo, distinguished himself in the descent on Heyang, and was transferred to Cang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 魏人立之，詔檢校工部尚書，領留後，進節度使，累加檢校尚書左仆射、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: The people of Wei installed him; edict appointed Honorary Minister of Works, acting governor, then military commissioner, cumulatively Honorary Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Associate Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wei installed him. An edict appointed him Honorary Minister of Works and acting governor, then military commissioner, and cumulatively Honorary Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Associate Counselor.

sentences.zh: 彥禎喜儒術，引公乘億、李山甫皆在幕府。

translations.literal: Yue Yanzhen favored Confucian learning; he recruited Gongcheng Yi and Li Shanfu into his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yanzhen favored Confucian learning and recruited Gongcheng Yi and Li Shanfu into his staff.

sentences.zh: 嗣襄王煴之亂，彥禎使山甫往見鎮州王镕，欲合幽、邢、滄諸鎮同盟拒賊，镕厚謝，卒不克。

translations.literal: During the turmoil of the successor Prince Yun of Xiang, Yue Yanzhen sent Shanfu to see Wang Rong of Zhenzhou, wishing to unite You, Xing, and Cang commands in alliance against the rebels; Rong thanked him warmly but ultimately could not agree.
translations.idiomatic: During the turmoil of the successor Prince Yun of Xiang, Yue Yanzhen sent Shanfu to see Wang Rong of Zhenzhou, hoping to unite the commands of You, Xing, and Cang in alliance against the rebels. Rong thanked him warmly but ultimately could not agree.

sentences.zh: 彥禎見王室微，頗驕滿不軌，大興其眾，城魏周八十里，一月畢，人怨其殘。

translations.literal: Seeing the royal house enfeebled, Yue Yanzhen grew arrogant and unrestrained; he massively conscripted labor to wall Wei for eighty li all around, completed in one month; the people resented his cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the royal house enfeebled, Yue Yanzhen grew arrogant and unrestrained. He massively conscripted labor to wall Wei for eighty li all around, completed in one month. The people resented his cruelty.

sentences.zh: 子從訓，資兇悖，劫王鐸，取其家，魏人不直。

translations.literal: His son Congxun, by nature fierce and defiant, plundered Wang Duo and seized his household; the people of Wei thought it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: His son Congxun, by nature fierce and defiant, plundered Wang Duo and seized his household. The people of Wei thought it unjust.

sentences.zh: 又聚亡命五百人，號「子將」，出入臥內，軍中藉藉惡之。

translations.literal: He also gathered five hundred outlaws, called the 'Prince's Guards,' who entered the bedchamber at will; the army murmured against them with loathing.
translations.idiomatic: He also gathered five hundred outlaws, called the 'Prince's Guards,' who entered the bedchamber at will. The army murmured against them with loathing.

sentences.zh: 從訓懼，易服奔近縣，彥禎即以為六州指揮使、相州刺史，輦兵械泉布，跡接於道，軍中益貳。

translations.literal: Congxun, afraid, changed clothes and fled to a nearby county; Yue Yanzhen immediately made him commander of six prefectures and prefect of Xiang, hauling weapons and coin along the road in an unbroken train; dissatisfaction in the ranks deepened.
translations.idiomatic: Congxun, afraid, changed clothes and fled to a nearby county. Yue Yanzhen immediately made him commander of six prefectures and prefect of Xiang, hauling weapons and coin along the road in an unbroken train. Dissatisfaction in the ranks deepened.

sentences.zh: 彥禎常夢解佩帶覆而行，既寤，曰：「此神告我，下將有背乎？」

translations.literal: Yue Yanzhen often dreamed his girdle and sash undone, walking bent over; on waking he said: 'Is this the gods warning me that subordinates will betray me?'
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yanzhen often dreamed his girdle and sash undone, walking bent over. On waking he said, 'Is this the gods warning me that subordinates will betray me?

sentences.zh: 已而軍亂，果囚彥禎，迫為桑門，尋殺之，推大將趙文㺹總留後。

translations.literal: Soon the army mutinied; they imprisoned Yue Yanzhen, forced him to become a monk, then killed him, and pushed the great general Zhao Wen'gao to oversee affairs as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the army mutinied. They imprisoned Yue Yanzhen, forced him to become a monk, then killed him, and pushed the great general Zhao Wen'gao to oversee affairs as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 從訓求救於朱全忠，全忠為起師，次內黃。

translations.literal: Congxun begged Zhu Quanzhong for rescue; Quanzhong raised an army and halted at Neihuang.
translations.idiomatic: Congxun begged Zhu Quanzhong for rescue. Quanzhong raised an army and halted at Neihuang.

sentences.zh: 從訓自相州以軍三萬傅城，文㺹不敢出，眾懼，殺之，更推羅弘信帥軍。

translations.literal: Congxun marched from Xiang Prefecture with thirty thousand men to press the city; Wen'gao dared not sally forth; the men, afraid, killed him and instead proclaimed Luo Hongxin to lead the army.
translations.idiomatic: Congxun marched from Xiang Prefecture with thirty thousand men to press the city. Wen'gao dared not sally forth. The men, afraid, killed him and instead proclaimed Luo Hongxin to lead the army.

sentences.zh: 弘信出戰，從訓敗，裒餘眾壁洹水，弘信遣將程公佐擊斬之，梟首軍門，實文德元年。

translations.literal: Hongxin rode out to battle; Congxun was defeated, gathered remaining troops and fortified at Huan River; Hongxin sent General Cheng Gongzuo to strike and behead him; his head was displayed at the army gate; this was the first year of Wende.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin rode out to battle. Congxun was defeated, gathered his remaining troops, and fortified at the Huan River. Hongxin sent General Cheng Gongzuo to strike and behead him; his head was displayed at the army gate. This was the first year of Wende.

sentences.zh: 彥禎起，凡七年。

translations.literal: From Yue Yanzhen's rise, seven years in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Yue Yanzhen's rise to his fall, seven years in all.

sentences.zh: 羅弘信，字德孚，魏州貴鄉人。

translations.literal: Luo Hongxin, styled Defu, native of Guixiang in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Hongxin, styled Defu, was a native of Guixiang in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，狀貌雄偉。

translations.literal: Skilled in horsemanship and archery, imposing in appearance.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in horsemanship and archery and imposing in appearance.

sentences.zh: 為裨將，主馬牧。

translations.literal: He was a deputy general in charge of horse pasturage.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a deputy general in charge of horse pasturage.

sentences.zh: 魏有巫告弘信曰：「白頭老人使謝君，君當有是地。」

translations.literal: A Wei shaman told Hongxin: 'A white-haired old man sends his thanks—you shall have this territory.'
translations.idiomatic: A Wei shaman told Hongxin, 'A white-haired old man sends his thanks—you shall have this territory.

sentences.zh: 弘信曰：「神欲危我耶？」

translations.literal: Hongxin said: 'Does the god mean to endanger me?'
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin said, 'Does the god mean to endanger me?'

sentences.zh: 文㺹死，眾曰：「孰願主吾軍者？」

translations.literal: When Wen'gao died, the crowd said: 'Who is willing to lead our army?'
translations.idiomatic: When Wen'gao died, the crowd said, 'Who is willing to lead our army?'

sentences.zh: 弘信輒曰：「神命我矣！」

translations.literal: Hongxin at once said: 'The god has commanded me!'
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin at once said, 'The god has commanded me!'

sentences.zh: 眾環視，以為宜，遂立之。

translations.literal: The crowd looked around one another, deemed him suitable, and installed him.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd looked around one another, deemed him suitable, and installed him.

sentences.zh: 詔擢知留後，再遷節度使，加檢校司空、同中書門下平章事、豫章郡公。

translations.literal: An edict promoted him to acting governor, then military commissioner, adding Honorary Grand Master of Works, Associate Counselor, and Duke of Yuzhang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted him to acting governor and then military commissioner, adding Honorary Grand Master of Works, Associate Counselor, and Duke of Yuzhang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠討黃巢，餉粟三萬斛、馬二百匹。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong campaigning against Huang Chao, he supplied thirty thousand bushels of grain and two hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Quanzhong campaigned against Huang Chao, Hongxin supplied thirty thousand bushels of grain and two hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 秦宗權亂，復詔弘信以粟二萬斛助軍，未輸，檢校工部尚書雷鄴來責粟，弘信素脅於牙軍，擅殺鄴。

translations.literal: During Qin Zongquan's disorder, again ordered Hongxin to supply twenty thousand bushels; before delivery, Honorary Minister of Works Lei Ye came to demand the grain; Hongxin, long intimidated by the yabing, had Ye killed on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: During Qin Zongquan's disorder, the court again ordered Hongxin to supply twenty thousand bushels. Before delivery, Honorary Minister of Works Lei Ye came to demand the grain. Hongxin, long intimidated by the yabing, had Ye killed on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 全忠以檄譙讓，弘信不敢報。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent a proclamation rebuking him; Hongxin dared not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent a proclamation rebuking him. Hongxin dared not reply.

sentences.zh: 大順初，全忠討太原李克用，遣將趙昌嗣見弘信假糧馬；

translations.literal: Early Dashun, Quanzhong campaigned against Li Keyong of Taiyuan, sent General Zhao Changsi to see Hongxin to borrow grain and horses;
translations.idiomatic: In the early Dashun era, Quanzhong campaigned against Li Keyong of Taiyuan and sent General Zhao Changsi to see Hongxin to borrow grain and horses;

sentences.zh: 又議屯邢、洺，假道相、衛，弘信不納。

translations.literal: also planned to encamp at Xing and Mo, borrow passage through Xiang and Wei—Hongxin refused.
translations.idiomatic: He also planned to encamp at Xing and Mo and borrow passage through Xiang and Wei. Hongxin refused.

sentences.zh: 全忠使丁會、龐師古、葛從周、霍存等引萬騎度河，弘信壁內黃，凡五戰皆敗，禽大將馬武等，乃厚幣求和。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent Ding Hui, Pang Shigu, Ge Congzhou, Huo Cun and others leading ten thousand cavalry across the river; Hongxin fortified at Neihuang, fought five battles all lost, captured great general Ma Wu and others, then sent rich gifts seeking peace.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent Ding Hui, Pang Shigu, Ge Congzhou, Huo Cun, and others leading ten thousand cavalry across the river. Hongxin fortified at Neihuang, lost five battles in succession, and lost his great general Ma Wu and others before sending rich gifts to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 方全忠圖河北，欲結納弘信，乃還兵。

translations.literal: Just as Quanzhong was scheming for Hebei, wishing to win Hongxin over, he withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Just as Quanzhong was scheming for Hebei and wished to win Hongxin over, he withdrew his troops.

sentences.zh: 全忠攻兗鄆，朱宣求援於克用，遣李存信率兵救之，請道屯莘，其下侵魏芻牧，弘信不平。

translations.literal: Quanzhong attacked Yan and Yun; Zhu Xuan sought aid from Li Keyong, sent Li Cunxin with troops to rescue, requesting passage to encamp at Shen; his subordinates raided Wei's fodder and pastures; Hongxin was indignant.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong attacked Yan and Yun. Zhu Xuan sought aid from Li Keyong and sent Li Cunxin with troops to the rescue, requesting passage to encamp at Shen. His subordinates raided Wei's fodder and pastures, and Hongxin was indignant.

sentences.zh: 克用欲合鎮、定兵營河曲，搤魏、滑路，弘信馳告全忠，請禁遊舸，絕往來。

translations.literal: Li Keyong wished to unite Zhen and Ding armies to camp on the river bend, choke Wei and Hua routes; Hongxin galloped to inform Quanzhong, requesting ban on patrol boats, severing traffic.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong wished to unite the armies of Zhen and Ding to camp on the river bend and choke the routes through Wei and Hua. Hongxin galloped to inform Quanzhong, requesting a ban on patrol boats and an end to river traffic.

sentences.zh: 久之，魏人不至，全忠疑其紿，自將至滑州。

translations.literal: A long time passed and Wei men had not arrived; Quanzhong suspected deception, personally led army to Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A long time passed and the men of Wei had not arrived. Quanzhong suspected deception and personally led his army to Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 弘信來告曰：「魏人未動者，正欲緩圖之。」

translations.literal: Hongxin came to report: 'The reason Wei men have not moved is precisely that they wish to plan slowly.'
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin came to report, 'The reason the men of Wei have not moved is precisely that they wish to plan slowly.

sentences.zh: 全忠遂屯曹。

translations.literal: Quanzhong then encamped at Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong then encamped at Cao.

sentences.zh: 太原將李瑭救宣，復壁莘，弘信厭其暴，而瑭溝壘自固。

translations.literal: Taiyuan general Li Tang rescued Xuan, again fortified at Shen; Hongxin loathed their violence, while Tang dug trenches and ramparts to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: The Taiyuan general Li Tang rescued Xuan and again fortified at Shen. Hongxin loathed their violence, while Tang dug trenches and ramparts to hold firm.

sentences.zh: 全忠遣使謂曰：「晉人誌並河朔，師還，為公憂之。」

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent envoy saying: 'The Jin people's ambition is to swallow Hedong; when our army returns, I worry for you.'
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent an envoy saying, 'The Jin people's ambition is to swallow Hedong. When our army returns, I worry for you.

sentences.zh: 弘信乃攻瑭，告全忠師期，全忠將趨滑為援，次封丘，而弘信已破瑭。

translations.literal: Hongxin then attacked Tang, informed Quanzhong of battle date; Quanzhong was about to rush to Hua as relief, halted at Fengqiu, but Hongxin had already broken Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin then attacked Tang and informed Quanzhong of the date of battle. Quanzhong was about to rush to Hua as relief and halted at Fengqiu, but Hongxin had already broken Tang.

sentences.zh: 克用怒，以兵掠魏博。

translations.literal: Li Keyong raged, sent troops to raid Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong flew into a rage and sent troops to raid Weibo.

sentences.zh: 全忠將侯言屯洹水，克用兵數求戰，言不敢出，全忠以葛從周代將。

translations.literal: Quanzhong's general Hou Yan encamped at Huan River; Li Keyong's troops repeatedly sought battle; Yan dared not sally; Quanzhong replaced him with Ge Congzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong's general Hou Yan encamped at the Huan River. Li Keyong's troops repeatedly sought battle, but Yan dared not sally forth. Quanzhong replaced him with Ge Congzhou.

sentences.zh: 從周為暗竇，每克用兵至，輒出精卒薄戰，必捷。

translations.literal: Congzhou dug hidden tunnels; whenever Keyong's troops arrived, he sent elite soldiers for close fighting, always victorious.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhou dug hidden tunnels. Whenever Keyong's troops arrived, he sent elite soldiers into close fighting and always won.

sentences.zh: 克用逾洹西北挑戰，從周大破之，禽其子落落，乃引去。

translations.literal: Li Keyong crossed northwest of Huan to challenge; Congzhou crushed him, captured his son Luoluo, then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong crossed northwest of the Huan to challenge him. Congzhou crushed him, captured his son Luoluo, and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 然侵魏不已，大戰白龍潭，弘信敗，克用追薄魏門而還。

translations.literal: Yet raids on Wei did not cease; great battle at White Dragon Pool; Hongxin defeated; Li Keyong pursued to Wei's gates and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yet raids on Wei did not cease. At the great battle of White Dragon Pool, Hongxin was defeated. Li Keyong pursued to the gates of Wei and returned.

sentences.zh: 弘信乃乞師全忠，全忠遣將壁洹水救魏。

translations.literal: Hongxin then begged Quanzhong for troops; Quanzhong sent general to fortify at Huan River to save Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin then begged Quanzhong for troops. Quanzhong sent a general to fortify at the Huan River to save Wei.

sentences.zh: 克用遊兵剽相、魏，民死十九，弘信不堪其逼。

translations.literal: Li Keyong's raiding cavalry plundered Xiang and Wei; nine in ten civilians died; Hongxin could not endure the pressure.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong's raiding cavalry plundered Xiang and Wei. Nine in ten civilians died. Hongxin could not endure the pressure.

sentences.zh: 光化元年，如全忠告亟。

translations.literal: First year of Guanghua, went to Quanzhong urgently pleading.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guanghua he went to Quanzhong to plead urgently for help.

sentences.zh: 全忠復遣葛從周將兵追躡，拔洺州，執其刺史邢行恭；

translations.literal: Quanzhong again sent Ge Congzhou pursuing, took Mo Prefecture, seized its prefect Xing Xinggong;
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong again sent Ge Congzhou in pursuit. He took Mo Prefecture and seized its prefect Xing Xinggong;

sentences.zh: 復攻邢，馬師素自拔走；

translations.literal: again attacked Xing; Ma Shisu fled on his own;
translations.idiomatic: again attacked Xing, and Ma Shisu fled on his own;

sentences.zh: 遂圍礠州，袁奉韜自殺。

translations.literal: then besieged Ci Prefecture; Yuan Fengtao killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: then besieged Ci Prefecture, and Yuan Fengtao killed himself.

sentences.zh: 不五日，取三州，斬首二萬級，禽其將百餘人，自是克用兵不出。

translations.literal: Within five days, took three prefectures, beheaded twenty thousand, captured over a hundred generals; from then Li Keyong's troops did not venture out.
translations.idiomatic: Within five days he took three prefectures, beheaded twenty thousand men, and captured more than a hundred generals. From then on Li Keyong's troops did not venture out.

sentences.zh: 始全忠亟討兗鄆，懼弘信貳，故歲時賂遺良厚。

translations.literal: At first Quanzhong urgently campaigned against Yan and Yun, fearing Hongxin's defection, so yearly gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: At first Quanzhong urgently campaigned against Yan and Yun and feared Hongxin might defect, so his yearly gifts were very generous.

sentences.zh: 弘信每有饋答，全忠引其使北面拜受，兄事之，弘信以為厚己，故推心焉。

translations.literal: Whenever Hongxin sent return gifts, Quanzhong had his envoys bow facing north to receive them, treating him as an elder brother; Hongxin thought himself honored, thus gave his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Hongxin sent return gifts, Quanzhong had his envoys bow facing north to receive them and treated him as an elder brother. Hongxin thought himself honored and thus gave Quanzhong his heart.

sentences.zh: 進累檢校太師，守侍中，徙臨清郡王。

translations.literal: Promoted cumulatively Honorary Grand Preceptor, Palace Attendant, transferred to Prince of Linqing Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted cumulatively to Honorary Grand Preceptor and Palace Attendant and transferred to Prince of Linqing Commandery.

sentences.zh: 光化元年死，年六十三，贈太師，追封北平王，謚曰莊肅。

translations.literal: Guanghua first year died, age sixty-three, posthumously Grand Preceptor, posthumously Prince of Beiping, posthumous Zhuangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Guanghua at sixty-three, was posthumously ennobled Grand Preceptor and Prince of Beiping, and given the posthumous name Zhuangsu.

sentences.zh: 子紹威襲。

translations.literal: Son Shaowei succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shaowei succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 紹威字端己。

translations.literal: Shaowei styled Duanji.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei, styled Duanji.

sentences.zh: 少有英氣，性精悍，吏事明辦。

translations.literal: Youth had heroic spirit, nature keen and hardy, clerical affairs clearly handled.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had a heroic spirit; by nature he was keen and hardy, and he handled administrative affairs with clear judgment.

sentences.zh: 既領留後，昭宗即詔嗣父節度，加累檢校太尉，號「忠勤宣力致聖功臣」。

translations.literal: Having received acting governorship, Emperor Zhaozong immediately issued an edict succession to father's commission, cumulatively Honorary Grand Preceptor, titled 'Meritorious Minister of Loyal Diligence and Sacred Service.'
translations.idiomatic: Once he received the acting governorship, Emperor Zhaozong immediately confirmed his succession to his father's commission, cumulatively ennobled him Honorary Grand Preceptor, and granted him the title 'Meritorious Minister of Loyal Diligence and Sacred Service.'

sentences.zh: 幽州劉仁恭引兵攻鎮、冀，遂掠魏，紹威告急於全忠，全忠自將與仁恭戰內黃，日中，大破之，斬首三萬級。

translations.literal: Youzhou Liu Rengong led troops attacking Zhen and Ji, then plundered Wei; Shaowei urgently appealed to Quanzhong; Quanzhong personally fought Rengong at Neihuang, at midday greatly defeated, beheaded thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong of Youzhou led troops against Zhen and Ji, then plundered Wei. Shaowei urgently appealed to Quanzhong. Quanzhong personally fought Rengong at Neihuang and at midday won a crushing victory, beheading thirty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 葛從周方守邢，亦敗其眾於魏縣。

translations.literal: Ge Congzhou was then guarding Xing, also defeated his forces at Wei County.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou, then guarding Xing, also defeated Rengong's forces at Wei County.

sentences.zh: 仁恭以眾十萬陷貝州，全忠使李思安屯內黃，從周悉軍入魏。

translations.literal: Rengong with a hundred thousand forces took Bei Prefecture; Quanzhong sent Li Si'an to encamp at Neihuang; Congzhou led entire army into Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong with a hundred thousand men took Bei Prefecture. Quanzhong sent Li Si'an to encamp at Neihuang, and Congzhou led his entire army into Wei.

sentences.zh: 仁恭攻魏，從周以五百騎出鬥，謂門者曰：「前有強敵，不可易。」

translations.literal: Rengong attacked Wei; Congzhou with five hundred cavalry rode out to fight, told gatekeepers: 'Strong enemy ahead, cannot be careless.'
translations.idiomatic: Rengong attacked Wei. Congzhou rode out with five hundred cavalry to fight and told the gatekeepers, 'A strong enemy lies ahead. We cannot be careless.

sentences.zh: 命闔扉。

translations.literal: Ordered gates shut.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the gates shut.

sentences.zh: 士死戰，執仁恭將二人。

translations.literal: Soldiers fought to death, captured two of Rengong's generals.
translations.idiomatic: His soldiers fought to the death and captured two of Rengong's generals.

sentences.zh: 仁恭使別將攻內黃，為思安所敗。

translations.literal: Rengong sent another general to attack Neihuang, defeated by Si'an.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong sent another general to attack Neihuang, but Si'an defeated him.

sentences.zh: 從周乘勝破八壁，追北至臨清。

translations.literal: Congzhou riding victory broke eight fortifications, pursued north to Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: Riding his victory, Congzhou broke eight fortifications and pursued north to Linqing.

sentences.zh: 仁恭乃還滄州，與李克用圖魏。

translations.literal: Rengong then returned to Cangzhou, with Li Keyong plotted against Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong then returned to Cangzhou and plotted against Wei with Li Keyong.

sentences.zh: 紹威與全忠連兵伐滄州，從周攻拔德州，進薄浮陽。

translations.literal: Shaowei with Quanzhong combined armies against Cangzhou; Congzhou attacked and took De Prefecture, advanced pressing Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei combined forces with Quanzhong against Cangzhou. Congzhou attacked and took De Prefecture and advanced to press Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 仁恭以兵至，監軍蔣玄暉請須其入壁，食盡可取。

translations.literal: Rengong arrived with troops; supervising commissioner Jiang Xuanhui requested wait until they enter walls, provisions exhausted then take.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong arrived with troops. The supervising commissioner Jiang Xuanhui requested that they wait until the enemy entered their walls and their provisions were exhausted before striking.

sentences.zh: 從周曰：「兵在機，機在上將，豈監軍所知！」

translations.literal: Congzhou said: 'War turns on timing; timing rests with the commander—how would a supervising commissioner know!'
translations.idiomatic: Congzhou said, 'War turns on timing, and timing rests with the commander. How would a supervising commissioner know!

sentences.zh: 逆戰老鴉堤，破之，斬首五萬，獲其將百餘人。

translations.literal: Met battle at Old Crow Embankment, broke them, beheaded fifty thousand, captured over a hundred generals.
translations.idiomatic: He met them in battle at Old Crow Embankment, broke them, beheaded fifty thousand men, and captured more than a hundred generals.
