sentences.zh: 又戰唐昌範橋，六遇輒勝。

translations.literal: Again fought at Tangchang Fan Bridge, six encounters all victorious.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again at Tangchang Fan Bridge and won six encounters in succession.

sentences.zh: 仁恭約和，乃還。

translations.literal: Rengong sued for peace, then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong sued for peace and then returned.

sentences.zh: 紹威德全忠，故奉事愈固。

translations.literal: Shaowei indebted to Quanzhong, thus served him ever more steadfastly.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei was indebted to Quanzhong and thus served him ever more steadfastly.

sentences.zh: 全忠遷帝洛陽，命諸鎮治宮闕，而紹威營太廟，加侍中，封鄴王。

translations.literal: Quanzhong moved emperor to Luoyang, ordered commands to repair palace halls; Shaowei built the Grand Temple, added Palace Attendant, enfeoffed Prince of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong moved the emperor to Luoyang and ordered the commands to repair the palace halls. Shaowei built the Grand Temple, was made Palace Attendant, and was enfeoffed Prince of Ye.

sentences.zh: 魏牙軍，起田承嗣募軍中子弟為之，父子世襲，姻黨盤互，悍驕不顧法令，憲誠等皆所立，有不慊，輒害之無噍類。

translations.literal: Wei yabing originated when Tian Chengsi recruited sons of officers for it; fathers and sons inherited in succession, marriage cliques intertwined; fierce and arrogant disregarding laws; Xiancheng and others were all installed by them; if displeased, killed without leaving a scrap.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei yabing originated when Tian Chengsi recruited the sons of officers for the corps. Fathers and sons inherited their places in succession, and marriage cliques intertwined. They were fierce and arrogant, heedless of law. Xiancheng and others were all installed by them; if displeased, they killed without leaving a scrap.

sentences.zh: 厚給稟，姑息不能制。

translations.literal: Generously supplied rations, indulgence could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: They were generously supplied with rations, and indulgence could not control them.

sentences.zh: 時語曰：「長安天子，魏府牙軍。」

translations.literal: Saying of the time: 'Son of Heaven in Chang'an, yabing in Wei's headquarters.'
translations.idiomatic: A saying of the time ran: 'The Son of Heaven in Chang'an, the yabing in Wei's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 謂其勢強也。

translations.literal: Meaning their power was strong.
translations.idiomatic: It meant their power was strong.

sentences.zh: 紹威懲曩禍，雖外示優假，而內不堪。

translations.literal: Shaowei learning from past calamity, though outwardly showing favor, inwardly could not endure.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei, chastened by past calamity, outwardly showed them favor but inwardly could not endure them.

sentences.zh: 俄而小校李公佺作亂，不克，奔滄州。

translations.literal: Soon petty officer Li Gongtuan rebelled, failed, fled to Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the petty officer Li Gongtuan rebelled, failed, and fled to Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹威乃決策屠翦，遣楊利言與全忠謀。

translations.literal: Shaowei then decided on massacre and purge, sent Yang Liyan to plot with Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei then decided on massacre and purge and sent Yang Liyan to plot with Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 全忠乃遣苻道昭將兵合魏軍二萬攻滄州，求公佺，又遣李思安助戰，魏軍不之疑。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent Fu Daozhao leading troops joining Wei army twenty thousand against Cangzhou seeking Gongtuan, also sent Li Si'an to assist; Wei army did not suspect.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent Fu Daozhao leading troops to join the Wei army—twenty thousand in all—against Cangzhou to seize Gongtuan, and also sent Li Si'an to assist. The Wei army suspected nothing.

sentences.zh: 紹威子，全忠婿也，會女卒，使馬嗣勛來助葬，選長直千人納盟器，實甲以入。

translations.literal: Shaowei's son was Quanzhong's son-in-law; when his daughter died, sent Ma Sixun to assist burial, selected thousand long-service guards bringing alliance vessels, actually armor inside to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei's son was Quanzhong's son-in-law. When his daughter died, Quanzhong sent Ma Sixun to assist with the burial. Sixun selected a thousand long-service guards to bring in alliance vessels that in fact concealed armor.

sentences.zh: 全忠自滑濟河，聲言督滄景行營。

translations.literal: Quanzhong himself crossed river from Hua, proclaiming supervision of Cang and Jing field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong himself crossed the river from Hua, proclaiming that he was supervising the Cang and Jing field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 紹威欲出迎，假銳兵以入，軍中勸毋出而止。

translations.literal: Shaowei wished to go out to welcome, borrow sharp troops to enter; army advised not go out and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei wished to go out to welcome him and borrow crack troops to enter the city, but the army advised against going out and he stopped.

sentences.zh: 紹威遣人潛入庫，斷纮解甲，註夜，將奴客數百與嗣勛攻之，軍趨庫得兵，不可戰，因夷滅凡八千族，市為空。

translations.literal: Shaowei sent men secretly into arsenal, severed bowstrings, unstrapped armor; at night led several hundred slaves and guests with Sixun to attack; army rushed arsenal got weapons, could not fight, thus exterminated in all eight thousand clans, market emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei sent men secretly into the arsenal to sever bowstrings and unstrap armor. That night he led several hundred slaves and retainers with Sixun to attack. The army rushed the arsenal for weapons but could not fight. Thus eight thousand clans were exterminated and the market stood empty.

sentences.zh: 平明，全忠亦至，聞事定，馳入軍。

translations.literal: At dawn Quanzhong also arrived, heard matter settled, galloped into army.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Quanzhong also arrived. Hearing the matter was settled, he galloped into the army.

sentences.zh: 魏兵在行者聞變，於是史仁遇保高唐，李重霸屯宗縣，分據貝、澶、衛等六州。

translations.literal: Wei soldiers on the march hearing change; then Shi Renyu held Gaotang, Li Chongba encamped Zong County, divided holding Bei, Cang, Wei and other six prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Wei soldiers on the march heard of the upheaval. Then Shi Renyu held Gaotang, Li Chongba encamped at Zong County, and they divided among themselves Bei, Cang, Wei, and four other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 仁遇自稱魏博留後，全忠解滄州兵以攻高唐，仁遇引眾走，為遊騎所獲，支解之，進拔博、澶二州。

translations.literal: Renyu styled himself Weibo acting governor; Quanzhong diverted Cangzhou army to attack Gaotang; Renyu led crowd fleeing, captured by patrol cavalry, dismembered; advanced took Bo and Cang two prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Renyu styled himself Weibo acting governor. Quanzhong diverted the Cangzhou army to attack Gaotang. Renyu fled with his followers, was captured by patrol cavalry, and was dismembered. Quanzhong then advanced and took Bo and Cang.

sentences.zh: 李重霸走，俄斬其首，相、衛皆降。

translations.literal: Li Chongba fled, soon beheaded; Xiang and Wei all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongba fled and was soon beheaded. Xiang and Wei both surrendered.

sentences.zh: 紹威雖除其逼，然勢弱，為全忠牽制，比州刺史矣，內悒悒悔恨。

translations.literal: Though Shaowei removed their pressure, yet power weak, controlled by Quanzhong, comparable to a prefectural governor, inwardly brooding with regret.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shaowei had removed their pressure, his power was now weak. Controlled by Quanzhong, he was little more than a prefectural governor, and brooded inwardly with regret.

sentences.zh: 全忠兵在滄州，紹威主饋免，自鄴至長蘆五百里，不絕於道。

translations.literal: Quanzhong's army at Cangzhou, Shaowei personally supplied provisions, from Ye to Changlu five hundred li, unceasing on the road.
translations.idiomatic: While Quanzhong's army was at Cangzhou, Shaowei personally supplied provisions along five hundred li from Ye to Changlu without cease.

sentences.zh: 全忠還，紹威建元帥行府，極土木壯麗，全忠大悅。

translations.literal: Quanzhong returned; Shaowei built grand marshal field headquarters, utmost splendor in earthworks; Quanzhong greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanzhong returned, Shaowei built a grand marshal's field headquarters of the utmost splendor in earthworks. Quanzhong was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 紹威間說曰：「邠、岐、太原皆狂譎，以復唐室為言。

translations.literal: Shaowei privately counselled: 'Bin, Qi, Taiyuan are all mad and deceitful, speaking of restoring the Tang house.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei privately counselled him, 'Bin, Qi, and Taiyuan are all mad and deceitful, speaking of restoring the Tang house.

sentences.zh: 王宜自取神器，專天下之望。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should yourself take the sacred vessel, monopolize the realm's hopes.'
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should yourself take the sacred vessel and monopolize the hopes of the realm.

sentences.zh: 全忠歸，乃受禪。

translations.literal: Quanzhong returned, then accepted abdication.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong returned and then accepted the abdication.

sentences.zh: 紹威多聚書，至萬卷。

translations.literal: Shaowei gathered many books, reaching ten thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei gathered many books, reaching ten thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 江東羅隱工為詩，紹威厚幣結之，通譜系昭穆，因目己所為詩為「偷江東集」雲。

translations.literal: Jiangdong Luo Yin skilled at poetry; Shaowei with rich gifts befriended him, linked genealogies; thus titled his own poems 'Collection Stolen from Jiangdong.'
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yin of Jiangdong was skilled at poetry. Shaowei befriended him with rich gifts, linked their genealogies, and thus titled his own poems 'Collection Stolen from Jiangdong.'

sentences.zh: 贊曰：田承嗣幾禽矣，李寶臣怒承倩而釋魏。

translations.literal: Commentary: Tian Chengsi nearly captured; Li Baozhen angered at Cheng Qian yet released Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Tian Chengsi was nearly captured; Li Baozhen, angered at Cheng Qian, yet released Wei.

sentences.zh: 建中之際，三將軍持銳躪血，功無成者。

translations.literal: At Jianzhong era, three generals wielded sharp blades treading blood, achievements none completed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time of Jianzhong, three generals wielded sharp blades and trod through blood, yet none completed their achievement.

sentences.zh: 四叛連勢，兵結難作，天子不能守宗廟。

translations.literal: Four rebels linked power, armies knotted calamity arose, Son of Heaven could not guard ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Four rebels linked their power, armies knotted and calamity arose, and the Son of Heaven could not guard the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 傳及弘正，去汙入朝，數年復亂，唐終不得魏。

translations.literal: Passed to Hongzheng, left stain entered court, within years again chaos, Tang ultimately never obtained Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Power passed to Tian Hongzheng, who left his stain behind to enter court; within years chaos returned, and Tang ultimately never regained Wei.

sentences.zh: 與夫豎刁亂齊，孰為輕重？

translations.literal: Compared with Shu Diao disrupting Qi, which is lighter or heavier?
translations.idiomatic: Compared with Shu Diao's disruption of Qi, which was the greater calamity?
